name: Kiwi Rootbeer
description: Kiwi Rootbeer blends soda-shop nostalgia with neon-candy tang, uniting (Rootbeer Freeze x Red Velvet S1) with Kiwi Sours from Alien Genetics. Crack the jar and you get a wave of vanilla-cream and sarsaparilla from the Rootbeer line, quickly cut by bright citrus-lime and tropical candy from the Kiwi Sours side; on the palate those impressions resolve into vanilla, cream, and citrus with a clean, fizzy finish. A balanced hybrid in the garden, it holds a medium stature with sturdy laterals and tight internodes, stacking frosty, calyx-rich colas that finish in about eight weeks indoors. Dominant terpenes commonly noted across the parents — limonene, myrcene, and caryophyllene — steer an upbeat, social effect: expect an initial lift and spark of energy that settles into a relaxed, happy calm. Potency trends THC-forward while CBD remains minimal, and yields are solid when the canopy is opened for light and airflow. The Red Velvet S1 component can push dessert-like aromatics and color, while Kiwi Sours — selected and refined by Alien Genetics — adds sour-candy clarity and speed. For growers and phenohunters chasing root-beer float nostalgia with modern lime-candy zest, Kiwi Rootbeer delivers a vivid confectionary profile wrapped in reliable, eight-week performance. Expect vigorous rooting, easy training, and dense, sugar-dusted flowers that cure into a smooth, dessert-leaning bouquet.

name: Blackout Truffle
description: Blackout Truffle hits the room before you see it: a pungent wave of chem, pepper, and diesel that hints at the brute resin output waiting inside its dense, dark olive bracts. Bred by Terp Fi3nd, this indica-leaning hybrid unites Bio Chem with White Cherry Truffle, marrying classic Chemdawg bite and Sensi Star heft to the truffle line’s deeper, musky sweetness. Expect compact, medium-height plants that stretch modestly, stack tight calyxes, and frost up early; by day 65–75 of bloom, colas wear a glassy coat of trichomes and rust-red stigmas that make trimming sticky work. Blackout Truffle is known for a forceful onset that hushes the chatter and melts posture, trading chatter for a slow, heavy focus and eventually heavy lids; THC potential is high while CBD remains low, and the dominant terpene duo of myrcene and caryophyllene drives the spicy, earthy finish behind the chemical top note. Indoors it delivers medium yields; outdoors, given long, bright days, it leans heavy. Growers prize its straightforward temperament and consistent structure as much as its cured bouquet: chemical and diesel up front, pepper through the mid-palate, and a lingering earthy echo that outlasts the last ember. Under proper drying and cure, its buds glint silver and violet, breaking to a room-filling mix of solvent, spice, and forest floor.

name: Princess Orange
description: Princess Orange marches into the garden with candy-shop swagger, a Shuga Seeds original that pairs the mother Orange Push Pop x Sherb Bx1 with the in-house stud Waifu. Her indica-leaning frame (about 70/30) stacks early and dense, pushing mint-green colas laced with bright tangerine pistils and a heavy coat of frost. Crack a cured jar and the room blooms with acid orange and ripe mango over a ribbon of strawberry, a fruit-forward bouquet that carries cleanly through the grind and finish. On the palate, the citrus pops first before rolling into creamy tropical sweetness, then settling into a long, sherb-kissed aftertaste. Expect a confident, high-potency ride - Princess Orange routinely tests in the upper tier (roughly 28-32% THC) - delivering a buoyant, euphoric lift that eases into a calm, body-forward glow without dulling the mood. Indoors she wraps in 55-65 days with a reliably heavy yield; outdoors she holds a compact, medium stature that responds well to light training and consistent feed. Growers call the workflow medium-difficulty: a steady environment rewards you with tight, crystalline tops and minimal larf. For anyone chasing saturated fruit terps and production in the same tent, Princess Orange proves that dessert flavors and real farm weight can live in one cultivar.

name: Zeelosa
description: Zeelosa marries candy-sweet Zkittlez from Dying Breed with Shuga Seeds' own Celosa (Gelato 41 x Sunset Sherbet Bx1), delivering an indica-leaning profile that looks as decadent as it smells. Expect dense, resin-caked colas that finish in roughly 63-65 days, stacking compact indoors and rewarding attentive growers with medium to high yields. The bouquet leans confectionary: grape and melon over a sugared backbone, with a faint ribbon of gas from its dessert lineage. On the palate it stays true - sweet, fruity, and tropical - before a soothing, body-forward high settles in. The experience skews relaxing and euphoric, often drifting toward drowsy as the session deepens, while the head remains calm and unhurried. Celosa's West Coast pedigree contributes structure and color, while Zkittlez keeps the fruit front and center; together they craft a terpene expression reminiscent of limonene, caryophyllene, and a touch of linalool. THC dominance is the rule here, with little CBD expected. Indoors, plants prefer stable environments and strong light to push the frost; outdoors, they shine where late-season weather stays dry. Bred by Shuga Seeds in collaboration with Dying Breed, Zeelosa reads like a modern classic - sweet, loud, and irresistibly resinous - perfect for growers and aficionados chasing a candy-coated finish and a satisfyingly tranquil unwind.

name: Madame Jelly
description: Bred by Shuga Seeds, Madame Jelly pairs the enigmatic French Breakfast with the studio's hash-star Waifu (Randy Marsh x Ice Cream Mints), yielding a dessert-leaning hybrid with serious resin credentials. Expect dark, tightly stacked flowers that frost over early and finish with a striking contrast of white trichomes on deep purples - typical of the Waifu side. In the jar and grinder, aromas tilt sweet and creamy with butter-cookie tones and ripe melon layered over a faint hit of diesel; that profile carries to the palate in a fruity, silky draw with a gassy snap on the exhale. Growers can anticipate vigorous, indica-forward structure, a cooperative stretch, and dense, extract-friendly calyxes; in controlled rooms the line commonly wraps in 65 days of bloom and rewards with heavy yields when light intensity and airflow are dialed. Potency trends high from the Waifu lineage, and the effect lands like a happy, body-forward calm that smooths edges without flattening mood - euphoric, relaxed, and sociable rather than sleepy. If you want a cultivar that presses beautifully, keeps jars fragrant, and looks as decadent as it smells, this is a standout from Shuga's catalog.

name: Jackee Robinson

Effects arrive quickly: an uplifted, creative spark and social clarity glide into a soothing, body-light relaxation that stays functional rather than couchy. Seed Junky's feminized release honors its namesake with precision breeding and repeatable performance.

name: Grape Waifu
description: Shuga Seeds’ Grape Waifu stitches together the grape-driven mother Grapes and the lavish hash-leaning father Waifu, yielding an indica-dominant hybrid (70/30) that stacks heavy, resin-caked colas with an elegant, upright posture. In bloom, notes of fresh grape and ripe melon lead, underpinned by a spicy‑diesel wink inherited from Waifu; the bouquet deepens as the flowers cure, trading topnotes of candied fruit for a silkier, bakery-leaning sweetness. Expect a generous harvest — listed as heavy — after 55 to 65 days of flowering, with THC commonly reported in the 25–28% range and negligible CBD. Grape Waifu’s structure favors dense, shimmering flowers and sturdy, mid-height branching that respond well to light training and airflow management. On the palate, grape and melon return alongside a peppery, herbal snap and a faint line of gas, while the effect trends classic indica‑leaning: a calm, euphoric lift that smooths into easy contentment and bright mood. A collab release between Shuga Seeds and Designer Genetics, Grape Waifu captures the decadent fruit of Grapes and the glossy resin and exotic nose of Waifu in a single, showpiece cultivar—expressive enough for top‑shelf flower and sticky enough for solventless work. Medium height indoors or out, it thrives under careful defoliation, rewarding dialed‑in gardeners with spectacular frost and camera‑ready color.

name: Permanent Waifu
description: Permanent Waifu by Shuga Seeds is a mostly indica hybrid that marries the award‑magnet lineage of Permanent Marker with Shuga’s own Waifu. Expect robust, compact flowers that finish in 55–65 days and stack heavily, reflecting the breeder’s “heavy” yield note. Aroma and flavor lean into diesel, gelato, fruity candy and a creamy vanilla finish, with some phenotypes hinting at Waifu’s melon influence. While the effect trends classic indica‑leaning: a calm, euphoric lift that smooths into easy contentment and bright mood. The structure tends to be squat‑to‑medium in height, with thick, resin‑frosted buds that make trimming rewarding. Reported THC potential runs very high (around 28–32%), while CBD remains minimal, placing this cross firmly in modern, potency‑forward territory. name: HashBurger 2.0
description: HashBurger 2.0 (HashBurger S1) refines a modern classic into a uniform, resin-first expression from California Seedbank's Mr. & Mrs. Respect. Selfed from the original HashBurger, itself forged by Han Solo Hash Plant x Double Burger, this 60/40 indica-leaning hybrid stacks dense, golf-ball colas on a medium frame with vigorous lateral branching and heavy trichome coverage. The nose hits with greasy burger funk - skunk, diesel, and peppery herbs - before unfolding earthy depth; caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene lead the terpene chorus with accents of humulene. Expect high production of sandy, easily collected resin heads and flowering that wraps in about 56-63 days. In the jar the buds glint silver and lime; on the palate the profile leans diesel-savory with spicy herbal edges and a lingering skunk sweetness. Potency runs heavy, with THC often in the upper 20s and capable of pushing into the low-to-mid 30s, while CBD remains trace. Effects land quickly yet smoothly, relaxed and happy with a mellow euphoria that settles body and mind. Dominant terpenes typically test as beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene, with measurable humulene; total cannabinoids can soar, while flowering stays manageable for commercial rooms.

name: Peach Burger
description: Peach Burger from California Seedbank marries the candy-bright uplift of Peach Oz with the savory, fuel-soaked depth of HashBurger, a burger-line champion. Bred by Mr. & Mrs. Respect, this hybrid greets the senses with sun-warmed stone fruit layered over lemon zest, diesel, and a faint peppery hash. Dense, frosted calyxes stack into sturdy, OG-style cones that trim cleanly and show excellent resin coverage for flower or rosin work. Limonene and caryophyllene lead the terp parade, with supporting myrcene rounding out a sweet-meets-savory profile that lingers on the palate. Expect a euphoric, mood-bright lift that settles into an easy, body-light calm - focused enough for daytime creativity yet relaxed enough for late-evening wind-down. THC expression is typically robust with only trace CBD. In the room and the jar, Peach Burger projects ripe-peach aromatics riding on citrus and gas. Growers can anticipate a vigorous, hungry plant that finishes in roughly 56-63 days of flower, with high yields when canopy and airflow are dialed. Credit where due: HashBurger's lineage has earned high-profile accolades, and in this cross it supplies the structure, vigor, and unmistakable funk, while Peach Oz paints the top notes in velvet peach. Balanced, bright, and undeniably loud - this is Peach Burger.

name: Sour HashBurger
description: Sour HashBurger fuses two titans of modern cannabis: the iconic Sour Diesel and the resin-laden HashBurger, brought together by California Seedbank. In the garden it shows hybrid vigor, stretching with strong laterals and stacking dense, sandy trichomes that nod to its hash-friendly heritage. Aromas lead with classic fuel and bright sour lemon over pine and pepper, a terpene medley often driven by caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene. Flavors echo the nose: tart citrus-diesel on the inhale, finishing with earthy pine and a savory flicker from the Burger side. Expect an upbeat, head-clearing lift that inspires focus and creativity before settling into a calm, content body ease; phenotypes lean THC-forward with only trace CBD, consistent with the lineage. Indoors under 12/12, many cuts mature in roughly 8 to 10 weeks, rewarding attentive feeding and airflow with generous yields; outdoors, tall frame and sturdy branching make trellising a smart call. Growers report medium-to-high yields of lime-to-olive flowers dusted in frost, with bag appeal that pops against a white backdrop. Credit to California Seedbank for distilling old-school diesel energy into a contemporary, extractor-friendly hybrid that still smokes like top-shelf flower. If you have been hunting for bright sour gas wrapped in modern funk, this cross delivers it with confidence.

name: Breesh
description: Breesh from Boston Roots Seed Co blends the Florida-classic Triangle Kush with the breeder’s Chemistry line, yielding an indica-leaning hybrid tuned for rich OG character. Expect dense, oversized olive-green buds with dark purple flickers, burnt-orange hairs, and a frosty coat of fine trichomes that hint at its 22–25% THC and trace CBD. The nose rides bright lemon over fresh pine and a subtle sweetness; on the palate those citrus-and-wood notes persist with a skunky, spicy edge. Myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene lead the terpene mix, translating to a profile that is both zesty and grounded. The experience opens quickly with a euphoric lift and loose, tingly warmth that settles into a happy, spacey calm without muting the strain’s flavorful finish. Plants show a classic OG frame with strong lateral branching and tight stacking; growers can anticipate a moderate challenge, medium indoor stature, and taller outdoor plants. Flowering typically wraps in 63–70 days, returning about 400-600 g/m² indoors and roughly 600 g per plant under the sun when well dialed. Breesh honors its lineage—Triangle Kush x Chemistry—by delivering modern bag appeal and timeless gas-citrus character shaped by Boston Roots’ selection work.

name: Cognac Black
description: Cognac Black pours a glass of classic Sour D swagger into Sherbanger's boutique berry-gas, then refines it under Bloom Seed Co's eye for structure and yield. From its parents, Sour D and Sherbanger, the latter a celebrated Boston Roots Seed Co creation from Sunset Sherbet x Headbanger, this sativa-leaning hybrid stacks conical, medium-tall plants that finish indoors in 9-10 weeks and swell outdoors by early to mid October. In the jar the nose is lively and layered: spicy citrus zest over ripe fruit with a creamy undertone, and a faint diesel snap as the lid cracks. On the palate, bright citrus and stone-fruit glide into soft cream, with a peppery finish that hints at caryophyllene alongside limonene and myrcene. Potency leans high in THC while CBD remains trace, matching its bright, head-first cadence. Growers can expect generous returns (around 650 g/m2 inside and up to 1200 g per plant outside) with firm, sugar-crusted flowers that trim clean. Effects land upbeat and lucid before easing into calm, a modern balance that reflects its lineage. Bred by Bloom Seed Co, Cognac Black preserves Sherbanger's boutique cut character while channeling Sour D's timeless edge, delivering a cultivar that feels familiar and new. Plants respond well to training and moderate feeding, with sturdy branching and internodal spacing that invites light and airflow.

name: Vitamin Sea
description: Vitamin Sea by Boston Roots Seed Co marries the candy-gas charisma of Apples & Bananas with the sherbet-fuel drive of Sherbanger, yielding a modern hybrid built for aroma as much as structure. Expect crisp apple and stone-fruit high notes wrapped in citrus zest and pine, with a diesel backbeat that lingers on the palate. Dense, frost-laden flowers often flash deep greens with occasional purple, a nod to both parents’ color potential. Caryophyllene, myrcene, and limonene take the lead in its terpene chorus, with a touch of linalool smoothing the edges. Reported effects skew bright and buoyant at the start — uplifted, happy, and lightly euphoric — before settling into a calm, content cruise that keeps the mind clear while the body unwinds. Indoors, flowering typically completes in about 56–70 days, and plants tend to stay at a manageable medium height with a steady, heavy yield when dialed in. THC potency lands firmly in the strong lane (often mid-to-high 20s depending on grow and cut), while CBD remains trace. Growers can anticipate resinous colas and easy trim thanks to tight calyxing.

name: Magic Ztrawz
description: Magic Ztrawz fuses Seed Junky Genetics' Magic Marker with Sour Ztrawz into a glossy, modern hybrid that smells like candy spilled across a gas station counter. The Marker lineage brings huge bling and dense, frost-caked colas, while Sour Ztrawz (Kush Mints x Zkittlez x Permanent Marker) layers bright sweet-sour fruit and a faint minty lift over solventy fuel. Expect medium stature with sturdy branching and quick, uniform flower set; most phenotypes finish in 8-9 weeks and can stack impressively, translating that resin output into high, market-friendly yields. On the palate it opens sweet, shifts to tangy citrus-sour, and closes with assertive diesel, making it a crowd-pleasing candy-gas profile. The effect trends balanced: an upbeat, euphoric start and clean uplift that settles into a calm, relaxed body tone without heaviness, ideal for creative focus or winding down. Potency is typically high with CBD minimal; exact numbers depend on cut and cultivation. Bred by Seed Junky Genetics, Magic Ztrawz carries the slick, photogenic bag appeal associated with the Marker family and packages it in a faster, grower-efficient frame. If you chase sparkling trichomes, bold aromatics, and reliable production, this cross delivers the kind of hybrid performance modern gardens are built around from seed to jar.

name: Permanent Cherries
description: Permanent Cherries blends candy fruit and marker funk into a standout modern hybrid from Seed Junky Genetics. Built from (Lemon Cherry x Kush Mints bx1) x Permanent Marker, its dense, sugar-dusted colas carry a 70/30 indica-to-sativa expression and a terpene trio led by trans-caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool. Crack a cured jar and the nose jumps from sweet citrus and cherry to mint and diesel-like gas, with a creamy undertone inherited from Kush Mints. The flavor follows through: tangy lemon, cool herbaceous mint, and a lingering fuel note over a sweet, dessert-style base. Typical lots test in a high-THC window of roughly 28–33% with trace CBD, translating to a potent, euphoric onset that brightens mood before settling into a calm, physically relaxing finish. Growers report a medium stretch and a straightforward, medium-difficulty run that flowers in about 56–63 days, with solid yields indoors and outdoors when canopy light is managed well. Buds finish deep green with orange pistils and a heavy frost. As a descendant of Permanent Marker, Permanent Cherries preserves that unmistakable marker funk while layering in bright fruit and mint from its Lemon Cherry and Kush Mints bx1 side; a flavorful, modern cultivar that stamps its name on the palate.

name: Lemon Ztrawz
description: Lemon Ztrawz steps out bright and unapologetic, a citrus-charged hybrid forged by Seed Junky Genetics in collaboration with Kushington. Built from Lemon Up and Sour Strawz, it leans modern sativa while keeping enough Kush backbone to steady the ride. Crack the jar and the room jumps: sharp lemon peel, sour-candy twang, and a faint earthy sweetness. On the palate, clean citrus and tangy zest dominate, with a subtle diesel echo on the exhale. Typical batches clock in from the low 20s up to the low 30s in THC, with CBD usually trace (often around 0.05%), delivering lively, clear-headed energy before easing into a calm, focused glide. Limonene leads the terp ensemble, backed by beta-caryophyllene, linalool, and myrcene, shaping that sparkling aroma and balanced finish. Plants tend to medium stature with sturdy lateral branching and frosty, lime-green colas tipped by amber pistils; expect a moderate yield and a fast 56–63 day indoor bloom. Growers report straightforward, moderate difficulty and best results with careful canopy management. However you meet it — in a jar or a garden — Lemon Ztrawz celebrates its parents: Lemon Up for the effervescent zest, Sour Strawz for the candy snap, and Seed Junky’s selection for the crystalline polish.

name: Funkberry Kush 2.0
description: Lovin In Her Eyes presents Funkberry Kush 2.0, a pungent, fruit-fueled hybrid born from Memberberry and Super Mega Fuego. It greets the room with a wild mash-up of aromas: think overripe orchard fruit splashed with propane, then a backbeat of berry, menthol, and a faint cheese funk inherited from its Fuego side. Medium in stature yet confident in structure, plants stack dense, resin-heavy colas and finish in 56–65 days, making the run brisk without feeling rushed. The profile leans candy-berry over fuel on the palate, with a diesel edge that lingers on the exhale. Expect a feel that opens bright and social before settling into a calm, happy cruise— relaxed, uplifted, and content — true to its balanced hybrid nature. While potency will vary by phenotype and environment, CBD tends to stay low as THC pushes the experience forward. The bouquet suggests a terpene mix led by caryophyllene with limonene and myrcene amplifying the sweet-tart fruit and gas. Yields are dependable when dialed-in, rewarding careful canopy management with sticky, easy-to-trim flowers. Crafted by Lovin In Her Eyes with their signature eye for flavor-forward crosses, Funkberry Kush 2.0 captures the nostalgia of Memberberry and the modern punch of Super Mega Fuego in one memorable harvest.

name: Cereal Milkshake
description: Bred by Umami Seed Co, Cereal Milkshake marries Cookies’ cult classic Cereal Milk with Umami’s own Zwish to create a dessert-forward hybrid that is both creamy and punchy. Expect a nose that opens with sweet cream and vanilla, layered with bright berry tones and a faint diesel ribbon from the Zwish side. Plants typically grow medium-tall with sturdy branching and dense, resin-packed calyxes that make for easy trimming and eye-catching bag appeal. Indoors, a dialed environment rewards growers with medium yields of frosty flowers in 8–9 weeks, and the resin quality makes this cross a natural pick for solventless exploration. Reported dominant terpenes often include limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene, supporting a flavor that lands between bakery-fresh and candy-coated. Effects lean balanced and buoyant: an initial lift in mood and perspective settles into a smooth, full-body calm without flattening focus. Potency tends to run high for this line, with THC frequently observed in the upper 20s (around 26–32%) and CBD typically below 1%. If you are hunting a modern hybrid that captures creamy cereal notes while keeping the profile vivid and gassy, Cereal Milkshake—born from Cereal Milk and Zwish—delivers exactly what its name promises.

name: Sour Sherb
description: Bred by SHERBINSKIS, Sour Sherb marries the electric tang of AJ Sour Diesel with the creamy depth of Sunset Sherbet, fusing old-school gas with modern dessert terps. Cracking a jar releases sharp diesel and lemon zest over sweet berry-cream, a profile often steered by limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene. The first puffs arrive fast and bright — euphoric, uplifted, and quietly creative — before easing into a smooth, body-light calm that keeps the ride focused rather than foggy. Dense, sugar-frosted calyxes stack into mid-height spears with lively orange pistils and a sticky hand feel. In the garden, this 60% sativa-dominant hybrid shows cooperative vigor and moderate difficulty, responding well to topping and light training. Indoors it stays medium in stature and finishes in about 7–9 weeks; expect generous yields around 10–12 oz per m². Outdoors, plants can stretch taller and are ready from late September into mid-October with 12-plus ounces per plant under good sun. Lab results on this lineage commonly land between 18–24% THC with trace CBD up to 1%, delivering satisfying potency without blunting flavor. Sour Sherb reflects Sherbinski’s California craft: heritage fuel brightened by sherbet silk, built for fans who want classic diesel energy wrapped in modern candy gloss. Expect smooth, clean burns and long-lasting, mouth-coating sweetness on the exhale.

name: Chocolate Bananza
description: Chocolate Bananza channels dessert-cart decadence into the garden, pairing Banana Kush with Chocolate Rainbow XXL in a Sherbinskis-bred hybrid that leans indica while keeping the lights on upstairs. From the Banana Kush side come tropical-sweet aromatics and a calm, happy tilt; the XXL parent, itself GMO x Gelato 41, layers silky cream and bright citrus over a faint diesel snap. Indoors, plants stay manageable, typically topping out near 70-110 cm with a slender, well spaced frame that welcomes SCROG or SOG. Expect dense, resin shelled colas and an XXL appetite for yield, with up to 600 g/m2 inside and roughly the same per outdoor plant when dialed in. Flowering wraps in about 60-65 days, finishing with swollen calyxes and vivid orange pistils. The effect opens euphoric and uplifted before easing into a smooth body melt that stays clearheaded enough for conversation. Typical THC lands in the high teens to mid-20s with trace CBD. Indoors it rates medium in height and difficulty, yet rewards attentive feeding and airflow. Expect an indica tilt around 65/35 and structure that builds a dominant central cola reliably.

name: Gasoline Sherblato
description: Gasoline Sherblato is Sherbinskis’ fuel-forward spin on dessert genetics, bred by pairing Sherblato with Fallout OG. From Sherblato (Sherbert x Gelato) it inherits creamy, sherbet-like sweetness and a lush, candy-citrus bouquet; Fallout OG layers in lime-zest brightness, pine, and a clear streak of diesel that earns the “Gasoline” tag. Expect a hybrid profile led by limonene, myrcene, caryophyllene, and pinene, translating to aromas of citrus rind, petrol, and vanilla cream. Plants will grow substantially during the flowering phase, resin-caked calyx stacks and strong lateral branching. Flowering completes in about 60–65 days, with capable growers pulling high indoor yields and higher outdoor hauls thanks to the compact, grape-like bud formation. In the jar, buds glisten with frost, releasing a gassy-citrus top note over a creamy, cookie-like finish. On the palate, bright lemon-lime and pine collide with rich gelato tones before a lingering diesel exhale. The experience balances body-loosening calm with buoyant mood and sparkle — relaxed, euphoric, and happy — though some users may note dry mouth, dry eyes, or occasional raciness. Gasoline Sherblato honors its parents while flying the unmistakable Sherbinskis flag for flavor-first, top-shelf hybrids.

name: Cherry Gas by Sherbinskis
description: Cherry Gas captures the sweet-candy sparkle of its lineage while delivering the calm, even-handed ride you expect from a true 50/50 hybrid. Created by Sherbinskis in collaboration with Sensi Seeds for the Breeding Grounds collection, this cross of Cherry Bacio (Cherry Bacio) and White Runtz (White Runtz) blends Kush (Kush), Gelato (Gelato) and Z genetics into compact, resin-stacked plants with a sturdy main cola and strong lateral branches. In flower, the room fills with cherry candy layered over creamy vanilla and sugar, with a faint diesel edge that deepens after cure; the flavor mirrors the bouquet with sweet, vanilla-laced pulls and a subtle gas finish. Effects arrive as a buoyant, talkative euphoria that sparks creativity before easing into a warm, relaxing body calm without heaviness. Indoors, Cherry Gas typically tops out around 70-110 cm and finishes in 60-65 days, yet still pushes XXL yields of roughly 460-650 g/m2; outdoors, plants can reach up to 200 cm and return as much as 550-750 g each in a sunny, Mediterranean climate. Expect dense, slightly conical buds dusted in a frosty coat with flashes of deep green and maroon from the Cherry Bacio side. Balanced, aromatic and generously productive, Cherry Gas is a polished showcase of the Sherbinskis x Sensi Seeds collaboration.

name: Purple Panties
description: Purple Panties by Sherbinskis marries Blue Sunset and Pink Panties into a vivid, fruit-forward hybrid with classic Cali pedigree. Expect an indica-leaning profile around 65/35 that layers a bright, heady lift over smooth, body-soothing calm. Aromas skew berry-citrus with a soft floral backnote; on the palate, ripe berries, sugared citrus zest, and light blossom echo through the exhale. Dominant terpenes regularly reported in the lineage-myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene-drive the sweet-fruity nose and rounded finish. Plants show robust, branching structure with dense, conical buds that can flash deep purples late in bloom. Indoors they reach medium-tall heights and deliver high yields near 500 g/m2; outdoors, well-run gardens can see about 550 g per plant. Flowering typically wraps in roughly 50-63 days. Potency trends into the mid-20s THC with trace CBD, producing an upbeat, euphoric onset that settles into clean relaxation without heaviness. True to its parents reputations-Blue Sunset (Sensi x Sherbinskis Breeding Grounds) and Sherbinski’s own Pink Panties-bag appeal is exceptional: frosted calyxes, orange pistils, and candy-fruit perfume. Bred by Sherbinskis, Purple Panties is crafted for growers and collectors who want saturated colors, dessert terps, and reliable performance in a compact window.

name: Jealousy Glaze
description: Born where dessert terps meet tropical funk, Jealousy Glaze stitches Papaya Jealousy and Gelato #33 into a modern Sherbinskis showcase. Its aroma opens with ripe papaya Jealousy (Jealousy x Papaya) for tropical density and creamy sherbet and soft cookie dough, then dries down to woody sweetness with a faint hint of pepper. Expect a balanced, upbeat onset that lifts mood and sparks conversation, settling into a calm, comfy body glow without heavy drag. Growers can expect tall, potentially unruly plants featuring an upright, robust main stem and thick, hearty lateral branches capable of supporting heavy, resin-soaked buds. In the right room, yields trend solid for both indoor and outdoor gardens. Caryophyllene leads the terpene stack, with limonene and myrcene rounding out the profile, mirroring the lineage: Papaya Jealousy (Jealousy x Papaya) for tropical density and Gelato #33 for that creamy, candy finish. While potency varies by cut and environment, batches typically land in the modern high range with minimal CBD. Jealousy Glaze carries the fashion-forward Gelato pedigree shaped by Sherbinskis, yet it feels distinctly new, trading syrupy sweetness for a brighter tropical cream. Whether you are pheno hunting or filling jars, this cross reads like a curated collaboration: expressive flavor, glittering resin, and crowd-pleasing, even-keeled effects. Developed with care, it rewards clean technique.

name: Dying Dream
description: Dying Dream, often seen as Dying Dreaming, is Seed Junky Genetics’ confectionary-minded cross of Bubble Gum and Gelato. The nose greets with pink bubble gum, rainbow candy and a gentle gush of sweet gas, while the flavor leans sweet and fruity with a faint diesel twang. Expect a buoyant, euphoric onset that stays lucid and creative before melting into a calm, relaxed body feel; many note an uplifting, dreamy headspace that lingers. Dense, resin-caked calyxes stack into lime-to-forest green spears brushed with tangerine pistils. Dominant terpenes typically show myrcene, caryophyllene and pinene, which map well to its candy, spice and pine sparkle. Potency runs high: lots test in the mid-20s, with reported ranges around 18.3–28% THC and trace CBD up to ~0.8%. In the garden, Dying Dream tends to medium-tall statures with compact branching; an 8–10 week indoor bloom finishes in frosty clusters. Given good light and airflow, growers commonly see generous returns — roughly 400–550 g/m² indoors and as much as 700 g per outdoor plant. Bubble Gum’s prizewinning sweetness and Gelato’s modern dessert pedigree meet here in a balanced, indica-leaning hybrid that delivers bright mood, smooth relaxation and standout bag appeal, all credited to Seed Junky Genetics.

name: Magic Pop Rockz
description: Magic Pop Rockz from Seed Junky Genetics marries LA Pop Rockz with Magic Marker, distilling modern dessert-gas character into a polished, head-turning hybrid. The nose opens with tart berry and confectioner's sugar over a sharp marker snap, then settles into diesel and earthy spice; on the palate it reads bright and sweet before finishing clean, with lingering berry-citrus zest. Dominant terpenes often include beta-pinene, beta-myrcene, and farnesene, supported at times by caryophyllene and limonene. Potency is unapologetic: batches commonly clock around 26-32% THC with trace CBD, translating to a vivid, fast-onset experience. The effect lands energetically at first: clear, focused, and uplifted, then evens into a calm, content cruise while preserving color and detail. Growers describe medium stature with strong branching, stacked calyxes, and dense, violet-speckled flowers that frost early. Indoors, phenotypes typically finish in about 56-63 days of bloom, with a reliable medium-to-high yield and standout bag appeal that keeps trimming satisfying. Everything about Magic Pop Rockz reflects its pedigree: LA Pop Rockz contributes candy-leaning fruit and structure, while Magic Marker layers in the unmistakable chemical-candy top note and resin density that define the "marker" family. The result is a modern hybrid that balances pop-candy aromas with confident power and a polished presentation.

name: Yuzu Sour
description: Yuzu Sour breathes new life into modern citrus profiles, a sativa-leaning hybrid bred by Compound Genetics by pairing (Orange Sherbet x OZ Kush F2) with Gastro Pop. Open a jar and bright notes of yuzu peel, orange sorbet, and sugared grape roll out over a kushy, diesel tinge; a floral lilac nuance lingers on the dry pull. On the palate it stays zesty and sweet before an earthy finish snaps clean. Expect a buoyant, functional high: a clear, creative lift arrives first, quickly joined by talkative euphoria and smooth body calm that never dulls focus. In California, select batches from top cultivators have shown THC in the mid-20s up to the high-30s with trace CBD, and the cut earned a runner-up nod for Best Citrus at the 2025 California Leaf Bowl. Dense, frosted colas flash violet and lime, a visual echo of its Orange Sherbet parentage, while Gastro Pop contributes that distinctive candied-grape gas. Dominant terpenes commonly reported include limonene, myrcene, and beta-caryophyllene. Growers describe the profile as rewarding yet exacting, with careful dialing needed to express the full citrus-grape spectrum. For connoisseurs chasing electric fruit layered with depth, Yuzu Sour stands out as a polished, modern classic. Its bright, sticky buds grind to an aromatic, sparkling fluff.

name: Egyptian Amber
description: Egyptian Amber by Compound Genetics pairs a zesty Yuzu Sour with the dark, gas-laden Black Amber, fusing citrus brightness with GMO x OZ Kush Bx2 depth. In the jar, aromas open with sharp citrus peel and yuzu candy before sliding into diesel, peppery kush, and a faint earthy cream. On the palate it is citrus-forward and clean, finishing with spicy-herbal fuel and a lingering mineral snap. Expect an upbeat, happy lift that sharpens focus while keeping the body calmly relaxed, a balanced profile that reflects its even 50-50 hybrid makeup. Growers can anticipate medium stature indoors and bushier frames outside; dense, resin-glossed colas hint at the heavy trichome output inherited from Black Amber. Flowering typically wraps in about 63 to 70 days, with indoor yields around 500 g per m2 and outdoor plants capable of roughly 800 g each under favorable conditions. Dominant terpenes often trend toward caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene, driving the citrus-diesel spice it shows in late flower. THC expression tends to be high with minimal CBD, and the cut's morphology rewards attentive training and airflow. Egyptian Amber credits Compound Genetics for the cross and showcases the line's knack for merging modern candy-citrus notes with classic gas, delivering a polished, production-friendly hybrid with memorably layered flavor.

name: Ridgeline Rose
description: Ridgeline Rose is a boutique cross from Ridgeline Farms that marries their powerhouse Lantz with Huckleberry Hill Farms' celebrated Whitethorn Rose, uniting candy-kissed gas with perfumed florals. Expect a vivid bouquet of rosewater, citrus zest, and fresh wood, underpinned by subtle spice; the flavor echoes with sweet petals and gently woody tones. Typically testing around 15-18% THC with negligible CBD, this indica-leaning hybrid (about 60/40) rides on a terpene stack often led by limonene, linalool, and caryophyllene. The experience opens bright and happy, settles into creative focus, and glides toward a calm, relaxed finish without losing social clarity. In the garden, Ridgeline Rose shows dense, resin-soaked calyxes with purple flecks and a tidy trim; indoors it generally finishes in 8-9 weeks and can deliver a dependable harvest when dialed. Lantz contributes structure, resin output, and the award pedigree that helped define modern Emerald Triangle genetics, while Whitethorn Rose lends color, elegance, and its unmistakable floral signature. Bred in Northern California's coastal mountains, its compact, vigorous frame stays manageable indoors and thrives outdoors. Growers note quick resin onset and a silvery cure that preserves the bouquet.

name: RIDGELION
description: Born in Humboldt’s rugged hills, Ridgelion by Ridgeline Farms pairs the candy-gas punch of Lantz with the tropical snap of Cheetah Piss to create a hybrid that roars from the jar. Aromas lead with citrus cream and sugared diesel before drifting into exotic funk; on the palate, a zesty citrus core rides over sweet fuel and faint florals. Potency typically lands between 25–30% THC with trace CBD, and the terpene trio is led by Limonene, Caryophyllene, and Linalool. Expect balanced, feel-good effects that brighten mood and focus without abandoning calm, easing into a smooth, relaxing finish. Growers will appreciate its easy, mold-resistant nature across environments; Ridgelion thrives outdoors, indoors, or under light-dep and piles on heavy resin over photogenic calyxes. Flowering wraps in about 8–9 weeks (roughly 56–63 days), delivering dense, frost-packed buds with Ridgeline’s signature bag appeal. The pedigree carries real pedigree: Lantz, a 2023 mixed-light champion, lends horsepower, while Cheetah Piss contributes that tropical bite and sneaky creaminess. Crafted by second-generation cultivators at Ridgeline Farms, Ridgelion stands as a flavorful, modern Humboldt hybrid built for showpiece jars, solventless washes, and dependable production runs, an assertive yet refined expression of California mountain genetics.

name: Platinum Lantz
description: Platinum Lantz by Ridgeline Farms marries the candy-coated lift of Ridgeline Runtz with the frost-heavy structure of Lantz, a celebrated Green Lantern x Ridgeline Runtz cross. Buds come deep purple and sugar-dusted, exuding sweet tropical-candy aromas over creamy berry glaze, gas, and pine. Caryophyllene, limonene, and humulene lead a terpene stack that reads loud and syrupy on the nose yet smokes smooth and clean. The high arrives fast and upbeat, euphoric, creative, and sparkling, before easing into a calm, full-body glow that keeps you functional and relaxed. Indoors, Platinum Lantz shows sturdy, medium-tall frames with rigid, nug-stacked branches and heavy resin coverage; expect generous returns from dialed rooms, with indoor harvests around the 500 g/m2 mark and outdoor plants finishing as broad, towering shrubs. Flowering typically wraps in about 63-70 days, with phenotypes expressing striking “platinum” trichome blankets late in bloom. Flavor holds true from dry pull to finish: a sweet, candy-forward start, berries-and-vanilla through the middle, and a lingering pine-fuel tail. Bred and selected in Humboldt by Ridgeline Farms, Platinum Lantz carries the same crowd-pleasing profile that won its parents Emerald hardware, refined into a modern, resin-rich hybrid that checks every box for jar appeal, aroma density, and balanced effects. Expect vivid bag appeal and excellent wash potential.

name: Lamboz
description: Raised in Humboldt by Ridgeline Farms, Lamboz fuses two standouts into one vivid hybrid: Lambo OG for classic gas, pine, and bright citrus, and Lantz for candy-grape sweetness, creamy undertones, and thick platinum frost. Expect noses of zesty citrus and conifer stacked over sugared grape and earthy Kush, with flavors that mirror the bouquet as the smoke turns sweet and lingering. Phenotypes lean from lime green to deep royal purple, building dense, resin-laden spears with a firm OG structure and abundant trichomes. The ride opens with an uplifting, euphoric clarity before easing into a calm, body-loosening cruise that melts stress without dulling the mood. In gardens, Lamboz shows sturdy branching and moderate stretch, finishing in roughly 8-9 weeks under mixed light or indoor setups with medium to high yields when dialed. A terpene profile led by caryophyllene and limonene, with supporting pinene, amplifies the gassy citrus-pine over candy notes. Potency is robust, reflecting its parents, Lambo OG and the Emerald Cup-winning Lantz, though exact THC/CBD can vary by cut and cultivation. Bred and selected by Ridgeline Farms, Lamboz captures Humboldt's modern craft: loud aroma, saturated color, and a balanced high tuned for good times and long views. Fans report a clear, happy headspace paired with a gently unwinding body.

name: Plantz
description: Plantz is a boutique Ridgeline Farms creation that marries Lantz with Purple GMO, bottling Humboldt hillside swagger in an indica-leaning hybrid. Deep purple, resin-lacquered colas push out grape gas and garlic funk, then resolve into sweet candy diesel on the dry pull. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene dominate the terpene stack, while THC commonly lands between 24 and 30 percent and CBD holds to trace. In outdoor beds and light-dep runs, Plantz stays vigorous yet manageable, stacking dense, hash-friendly flowers. It finishes in roughly 56 to 70 days, a tidy window for color chasers who will not compromise on structure. Expect medium height, sturdy branching, and a clean trim that reveals dense calyx clusters with minimal leaf. The ride opens with a bright, euphoric lift and settles into a relaxed, happy calm that keeps the mood buoyant without blunting character. Ridgeline's touch shows in the bag appeal: glassy trichomes over royal violet hues, a GMO-forward loudness refined by Lantz's Humboldt-bred candy gas. Growers prize its extract potential and photogenic finish; flavor hunters reach for its savory-sweet interplay when they want something unmistakably Humboldt yet thoroughly modern. Plantz proves why Ridgeline Farms continues to shape the Emerald Triangle's flavor conversation.

name: Throbber
description: Throbber from Ridgeline Farms fuses two of the Emerald Triangle's modern pillars into a dialed in hybrid. Its mother, Gush Mintz, layers cool mint and sugared candy over earthy citrus, while its father, Lantz, a Ridgeline cross of Green Lantern x Ridgeline Runtz, contributes sparkling purple coloration, rock hard structure, and that unmistakable candy pine snap. Green Lantern captured the 2018 Emerald Cup and Ridgeline Runtz brought home the 2019 Sungrown title, and Throbber feels like a victory lap: resin heavy, sticky sweet, and visually loud. On the nose it leads with mint and sweet confections edged by pine and a light gas note; the flavor tracks those layers cleanly, concentrating mint, sweet, and pine. The effect profile typically starts with a quick, euphoric lift and happy clarity before settling into a relaxed, steady body calm, consistent with an indica leaning hybrid. Growers can expect dense, frost caked colas that stack tightly; indoors, plants stay medium tall and respond to topping and trellis, while outdoor runs push vigorous branching and medium to high yields. Flowering falls within a classic hybrid window, and batches commonly show high THC with trace CBD, carried by a terpene mix often led by caryophyllene with limonene and myrcene supporting. Crafted by Ridgeline Farms in Southern Humboldt.

name: Purple Pineapple Express
description: Purple Pineapple Express is an indica leaning hybrid that delivers an energizing cerebral buzz and soothing sleepy body high. This Pineapple Express and Huckleberry Hound cross contains around 22% THC and a delightful fruity flavor, with a distinctly balanced experience that makes it perfect for hybrid fans. The effects of this strain are simultaneously uplifting and deliciously relaxing. Expect a happy cerebral rush that lifts the spirits and boosts mood, with a deeply soothing physical energy that moves through the body, making you more and more relaxed until you find yourself comfortably sedated and locked to the couch — likely very hungry and sleepy. These effects make Purple Pineapple Express a medical strain commonly used to support anxiety, stress, depression, PTSD, appetite loss, anorexia, and insomnia. It contains a tropical fruity flavor with a distinct pineapple taste that blends with woody pine, sweet berry, and grapes. The aroma is similar, but with heavier earthy and woody overtones and a sweet and tangy pineapple-berry finish. Growing Purple Pineapple Express can be a bit challenging, but will produce high yields of beautiful purple buds cultivated by growers with some experience. Flowering time is around 60 days, where it will produce dense dark green and purple buds with vibrant orange hairs that are dusted with sparkling trichomes.

Buds form dense, resin-glossed spears in deep lime greens with occasional violet flickers, reflecting vigorous growth and sturdy branching. Typical lab results place THC in the mid-20s with CBD staying trace, delivering a cheerful, uplifting onset that settles into a centered, creative cruise without heavy drag. In the garden, Chicken Dance was built for practicality: it shows strong vigor, forgiving structure, and a straightforward finish in roughly eight to nine weeks, rewarding dialed-in rooms or sun-grown terraces with notably high yields. Flavor tracks the aroma from first crack to last crumble, tropical fruit punch, citrus zest, and a faint pine-spice echo from its Green Lantern heritage, a celebrated Emerald Cup winner, all stitched together by Lantz’s dessert-leaning cream. Credit to Ridgeline Farms for a cross that feels both exuberant and focused: modern candy-tropical character with classic gas and structure, tuned for growers and post-harvest appeal alike.

The experience builds quickly: a clear, happy lift blooms into calm, full-body ease without fog, often leaving moods buoyed and conversation easy. Flowering usually wraps in about eight to ten weeks, and well-tuned runs can return medium-to-high yields. Caryophyllene, myrcene, and limonene commonly headline the terpene chorus, preserving that loud Humboldt gas. Ridgeline Rebel feels like a respectful salute to Emerald Triangle craft, modern polish built on proven winners, delivered with Ridgeline’s steady hand.

name: Rainbow Punch by Ethos

Growers appreciate its sturdy, indica structure and consistent stack, rewarding attentive dialing with resin-forward yields indoors or out. Primary aroma cues often echo fresh hops alongside citrus peel, a nod to the cultivar's limonene-forward profile. With a manageable canopy and cooperative internode spacing, it adapts well to topping, light defoliation, and screen training without drama. In short, this colorful hybrid channels dessert-tier aromatics with a spirited, feel-good shine born from two modern classics, in ETHOS fashion.

Outdoors, a stable, temperate climate keeps the OG side content and resin production high. Though the breeder is unknown, Yenzo's Cookies wears its lineage proudly, delivering the dessert-forward personality that made Girl Scout Cookies famous, polished by OG heft and structure. It is a balanced, modern hybrid built for growers who appreciate reliable morphology, classic flavors, and a satisfying, euphoric glide. Expect medium internodes, strong lateral branching, and dense, easily trimmable colas.

name: Woodzy

The buds cure into compact, resin-iced nuggets that snap cleanly from the stem, reflecting a phenotype that clones and grows very much like Z yet demands more attentive hands. The effect arrives quickly and heads-up: an easy euphoria and lifted mood that settles into a calm, happy glide without fog, making it a functional, evening-friendly hybrid with a distinctly indica-leaning feel. Woodzy's origin story is already part of NorCal lore, after turning heads in friendly contests and tastings, it joined Wood Wide's small-batch lineup alongside award-winning house work, proof of the team's careful pheno selection and meticulous indoor craft. If your palate gravitates to citrus, candy, and meadow-bloom accents with just a hint of gas, Woodzy delivers a clean expression of modern "Z" character in a more consumer-ready frame. Potency varies by batch, but expect a flavorful, premium indoor Z-style punch.

name: Limon-G

The profile trends lemon-diesel with flashes of citrus zest and faint earth, landing on the palate as tart, fuel-kissed citrus. The effect leans lively and upbeat, with many phenos described as happy, energetic, and brightly focused before settling into an easy, contented cruise. For growers seeking commercial reliability without sacrificing character, Limon-G delivers: fast enough to dodge shoulder-season weather, resinous enough for extraction, and expressive enough to keep connoisseurs returning to the jar. Bred and released by Twenty20 Mendocino, it is purpose-built for big, clean, lemon-forward harvests. Uniform structure from the below-average PVI makes canopy management straightforward and repeatable.

Typical lab results place THC from the high teens to mid-20s with trace CBD, driven by a terpene trio often led by beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene. On the nose and in the jar, those oils translate to a vivid, dessert-meets-fuel profile and sticky, frost-tipped buds. Effects tend to balance mood elevation and clearheaded ease with a calm, relaxing finish, reflecting its 60/40 sativa-to-indica lean. Credit to Twenty20 Mendocino for capturing classic Mendo cherry character and Smarties’ confectionary charm in a contemporary, garden-friendly hybrid that thrives under trellis, finishes with deep color in cooler nights, and shines as both whole flower and concentrate input.

For cultivators seeking a distinctive aroma without finicky support needs, PineRose offers a fresh, modern profile anchored to a practical 8½–9½‑week finish and a dependable, medium output—balanced genetics, thoughtfully executed. Expect dense, lime‑to‑olive flowers dusted in sparkling trichomes and a clean, garden‑fresh finish.

Indoors she races to finish in about 49-55 days, and outside she targets a mid-September harvest, delivering above-average yields per square foot while asking little in the way of trellising. The experience leans calm and heavy-eyed - relaxed, happy, and sleepy - echoing Bubba lineage, with a terp profile suggestive of caryophyllene, humulene, and myrcene. As part of Twenty20's early-finishing line, Honey Badger F7 contributes the speed gene without muting resin, so Early Bubba is as practical as it is flavorful: fast, stout, and built for shoulder-season success with sturdy structure and dependable uniformity. Growers also note a below-average need for support and a consistent canopy that makes trimming straightforward and efficient.

name: Cereal Berries
description: Cereal Berries distills Alien Genetics' cereal-and-soda nostalgia into a single cultivar. Also known as Rootbeer Pebbles F2, it is bred from Rootbeer Pebbles #7 crossed back to Rootbeer Pebbles, with Rootbeer Pebbles itself descending from Fruity Pebbles OG (F5) and Rootbeer BC2 F2 by Mean Gene from Mendocino. Expect dry flowers that smell like a bowl of berries set beside a vanilla cream soda: bright berry sweetness from the FPOG side, cushioned by creamy, sarsaparilla-like undertones from the Rootbeer line. Its balanced hybrid character leans social and upbeat—often described as happy, euphoric, and comfortably relaxed—without losing focus. Indoors, most phenotypes finish in roughly 8–9 weeks, reflecting the parental timing; yields trend moderate with dense, frosted nugs that show the Pebbles family’s colorful anthocyanin streaks. description: Strawberry Junky fuses Strawberry Pines with Cap Junky to create a modern hybrid that smells like fresh strawberry preserves spread over pine wood with a backdraft of peppered diesel. This cross inherits dense, calyx-heavy buds and a shimmering blanket of resin from the Cap Junky side, while Strawberry Pines contributes brighter red-berry notes and a crisp forest-clean finish. Expect a balanced profile, relaxing yet buoyant, with users commonly describing a relaxed, tingly lift that can turn giggly before settling into steady calm. In the garden, Strawberry Junky is a vigorous stretcher with medium stature indoors and higher reach outdoors; flowering wraps in roughly 60-70 days, and dialed rooms can produce dense, sticky colas with solid returns. THC levels are typically high, while CBD stays below 1%. Flavor carries through on the cure: ripe strawberry up front, fresh pine in the middle, and classic diesel on the exhale. Built from Strawberry Pines x Cap Junky, Strawberry Junky pairs boutique berry character with strong bag appeal in one polished package. Expect 600-700 g/m2 indoors in dialed environments.

name: Ultramarine
description: Ultramarine from Bodhi Seeds blends Blue Camphor (mother) with Lavender Lemonaid (father) to conjure a hybrid whose profile balances cool fuel and bright citrus. In the room, a lemon lavender potpourri swirls over a gassy backbone, finishing with a faint OG candy sparkle. Plants tend to stack tidy, resin-etched colas and finish quickly; most growers report a harvest window around nine weeks indoors, with finish times clustering near day 63 from flip. Expect aromas that translate directly to flavor, with zesty lemon peel upfront, sweet floral tones in the mid, and a diesel echo on the exhale. While lab numbers vary by selection, potency reflects modern hybrid standards and CBD is typically trace. Ultramarine was released as regular seeds, encouraging selection to find either the camphor-leaning mother’s cool spice or the father’s citrus-lavender candy lane. Yields track solidly in the middle in a dialed environment, and structure responds well to pruning and light training. For effect, users often describe a cheerful, uplifted, onset that settles into an easy, relaxed mood without heavy sedation. If you appreciate a citrus-forward bouquet with a floral twist and a succinct 9-week turnaround, Ultramarine’s elegant fusion of Blue Camphor and Lavender Lemonaid lands squarely in that sweet spot.

name: Chocolate Dragon
description: Chocolate Dragon unlocks a rare flavor corridor from Bodhi Seeds’ Yab Yum imprint, pairing White Chocolate (mom) with D’Soul (dad) for a poised hybrid that feels equal parts silk and spark. In the garden it moves with calm certainty, building sugar-frosted spears and chunky side colas, then landing squarely on a nine‑week finish, a tidy 63 days from flip for growers who like schedules as crisp as resin heads. Crack a jar and the greeting is unmistakable: green gas drifts out first, soon couched in creamy, confection-like tones and a warming thread of spice, a profile that reads diesel-tinged vanilla with pepper around the edges. The first impression in use is brightness—mood up, chatter easy—followed by a steadying exhale that softens shoulders without blurring focus, a happy, uplifted calm that lingers into a quietly relaxed glide. Plants show classic hybrid stature and a cooperative trim thanks to dense, well-formed bracts; with a bit of light and air management, they stack neatly and frost early. Chocolate Dragon doesn’t shout about numbers, it whispers with character: dependable timing, jar-friendly structure, and a flavor that keeps you double-checking the label. Credit to Bodhi Seeds for this elegant crossroads of comfort and spark everywhere.

name: Honey Beez
description: Honey Beez by DNA Genetics nods to the classic Honey Bee lineage, itself a Flo x Biker Bob cross known for its buoyant, citrus-forward profile. In this sativa-leaning hybrid (about 70% sativa/30% indica), aromas open with light honey and zesty citrus before deepening into ripe mango and an earthy undercurrent. Typical lab results place THC in the mid-teens (roughly 16-17%) with CBD that can approach 2%, setting an approachable ceiling that favors clarity over sheer force. On the palate, Honey Beez mirrors the bouquet: sweet honey, citrus oil, and tropical fruit. The experience trends upbeat and focused, with a confident, uplifted lift that keeps conversation easy and mood bright while the body unwinds in the background in a subtly relaxed way. In the garden, expect medium stature, steady internode spacing, and a cooperative temperament that rewards basic training with medium yields of firm, sugar-frosted flowers. While exact days to finish can vary by phenotype and setup, Honey Beez typically runs on a classic hybrid schedule, pairing efficiency with its lively terp expression. For fans of vintage DJ Short lines and modern refinement, this DNA Genetics selection packages familiar sunshine into a clean, contemporary cut. Expect dense calyx stacks, bright amber pistils, and a sparkling coat of trichomes that polish each nug's honey-tinted glow.

name: Santo
description: Santo from Bodhi Seeds pairs two charismatic parents to create a resin-rich, color-splashed hybrid with classic-meets-modern character. On the maternal side, Saint Stephen (formerly known as Stevie Wonder) blends Bubba Kush, Blueberry, Trainwreck, and Sensi Star, a medley famous for bubble‑gum berry notes, eucalyptus-leaning spice, and cheerful uplift. D’Soul supplies the counterpoint, tying Pine‑soul brightness to Dragon’s Blood hash‑plant depth for a foresty backbone and dense, frost-heavy flowers. Together, Santo leans into a bright citrus‑pine bouquet anchored by sweet berry, with effects that open upbeat and euphoric before settling into an easy, relaxed cruise. Plants typically reach medium height with sturdy arms and vivid autumnal hues late in bloom, stacking sparkling calyxes that cleanly trim. Indoors or out, expect medium yields of sticky, terpene-forward tops that finish in about nine weeks (roughly 63 days) once flowers set. While lab numbers vary by selection, Santo expresses a THC‑dominant chemotype with only trace CBD, and a terp profile often driven by limonene and pinene over a myrcene-tinged berry sweetness. Credit to Bodhi Seeds for uniting Saint Stephen and D’Soul so harmoniously—Santo feels familiar yet distinct, a thoughtful splice of vintage flavor, modern resin, and feel‑good, mood‑brightening momentum.

name: Choco Mintz
description: Choco Mintz from DNA Genetics leans into a dessert profile while carrying the depth of its Chocolate Mint OG lineage. DNA Genetics presents it as an indica-dominant hybrid, and while the underlying Chocolate Mint OG line is commonly associated in secondary sources with Emerald OG and Granddaddy Purple, that parent split is not reliably confirmed for Choco Mintz itself. Crack the jar and a cool wave of mint lifts over rich chocolate, grounded by earthy pine and a dusting of spice, while the profile reads sweet first, then resinous and woody. DNA Genetics lists this cultivar with THCa at 20%, delivering a soothing body high that feels euphoric and deeply relaxed without flattening the mood. The overall effect profile lands as evening-friendly and calming, with a gentle uplift that keeps the experience warm rather than heavy. Dense, frosted flowers and a cool chocolate-mint profile give Choco Mintz a polished, after-dinner feel. For smokers chasing classic West Coast depth with confectionery flair, Choco Mintz delivers a refined expression of Chocolate Mint OG lineage with a softly happy finish.

name: Penkiller
description: Penkiller is Exotic Seed’s purple-leaning collaboration with Nerone, uniting Permanent Marker and Biscotti Pink Champagne into a modern, resin-first hybrid. From the first rub of a cured nug, a bold bouquet breaks loose: gassy marker funk from Permanent Marker meets dessert-like sweetness from Biscotti, with creamy layers and a faint earthy echo. Plants build a balanced, medium-stature frame with tight internodes and heavy trichome coverage that paints calyxes in lilac and deep forest greens. Classified at 70% indica and 30% sativa, Penkiller carries very high potency; cannabinoid ratios vary by environment, but expression consistently trends toward robust THC with minimal CBD. Indoors it wraps in about nine weeks (roughly 63 days), and in temperate regions it finishes outdoors around October. Growers can expect dense, uniform colas and commercial output in the 500–550 g/m² range, responding well to light defoliation and support stakes late in bloom. In the jar and on the palate, its profile leans sweet cream and pastry over a diesel backbone, accented by hints of spice and soil. The high arrives smooth and assertive, uplifting at the onset before settling into a deeply contented, relaxed calm with a softly happy finish. Bred and released by Exotic Seed.

name: Turbo Junky
description: Turbo Junky from Exotic Seed compresses modern American intensity into a fast, compact photoperiod. Built from Cap Junky and Herz OG Auto, it leans 70% indica, pushing squat, resin-paved colas that often blush purple while staying dense and easy to trim. In the tent, it sprints from flip to finish in about 7-8 weeks, and trained canopies routinely hit 500-550 g/m2, with outdoor finishes landing by September in temperate zones. Expect an assertive nose that fuses diesel and menthol over fresh pine, a profile reflected on the palate and carried by a terpene backbone led by beta-caryophyllene, with limonene and pinene close behind. Reported potency hovers near 30% THC, placing Turbo Junky among the heavier hitters in the Exotic Seed lineup, yet its mood remains composed: a deep, body-forward calm paired with clear, upbeat undertones. Structure is compact with short internodes; buds dry to a frosty, silver-green finish, saturating jars with sharp, cooling aromatics. If you are chasing speed without sacrificing bag appeal or strength, Turbo Junky captures the Cap Junky ferocity and filters it through Herz OG Auto's efficiency, delivering a visually striking, terp-rich harvest on a schedule that rewards both diligent newcomers and seasoned dialers. Expect compact plants, vigorous resin production, and a clean, effortless trim.

name: Nal Nudda
description: From Exotic Genetix, Nal Nudda fuses Grease Monkey with Drippin' Aint Eazy into a photoperiod hybrid that stacks dense, resin-heavy colas and a head-turning gassy bouquet. The Grease Monkey side brings diesel punch and thick trichome coverage, while Drippin' Aint Eazy layers in creamy cookie sweetness and exotic gas, yielding an aroma that opens with diesel and earth, rolls through nutty vanilla, and finishes with a subtle spicy echo. Expect a balanced onset: a bright, uplifted focus that gradually softens into easy, full-body calm without couch-locking drift. Plants show medium-to-tall stature with strong lateral branching and vigorous flower set, finishing in about 56-63 days indoors and rewarding dialed environments with notably high yields. Sticky flowers glisten as they ripen, making Nal Nudda equally at home in jars or over screens for solventless pulls. Though cannabinoid numbers vary by cut and grow, this cultivar is typically THC-forward with negligible CBD and a terpene cast led by caryophyllene, myrcene, and limonene. Flavor mirrors the nose: diesel up front, creamy vanilla through the mid-palate, and a nutty, slightly herbal exhale. Bred by Exotic Genetix, Nal Nudda carries its parents' modern pedigree and production chops, delivering potency, bag appeal, and efficiency in a single, well-behaved package.

name: Jackfroot
description: Jackfroot from Nine Weeks Harvest brings a bright, fruit-stand twist to modern candy-gas genetics by pairing Madd Fruit with Runtz. The bouquet opens with tropical sweetness and citrus zest over a creamy sugar note, then dries down to a light earthy finish. In the garden, Jackfroot tends to stack medium-height spears with strong laterals and dense, resin-crusted calyxes, a nod to Runtz's bag appeal and the juicy, tart character of its Maad Fruit parent. Expect a balanced hybrid ride that lifts mood and focus before settling into a smooth, body-light calm; tasters commonly report euphoric, happy, and relaxed vibes with a classic candy aftertaste. Indoors, most cuts aim for a swift finish around eight to nine weeks of bloom, and well-managed plants reward with medium yields of frosty, sticky flowers that trim cleanly. Flavor carries through to the palate: sweet tropical candy, citrus, and a hint of vanilla, making Jackfroot an easy choice for jar rotation. Bred and released by Nine Weeks Harvest, this cross captures the brand's nine-week ethos without sacrificing richness or color, offering a vivid, fruit-forward profile married to modern potency and showpiece structure. Its architecture shows compact internodes and stout, supportive branches that handle dense flower weight. Trichome coverage is heavy, making Jackfroot attractive for dry-sift and rosin work.

name: Tropiburger
description: Tropiburger from Nine Weeks Harvest fuses the savory Hash Burger with bright Trop Cherry to deliver an orange-citrus lane built for real-world production. In the garden it shows a tall frame with firm laterals, sensible internode spacing, and stacked, spear-like colas that harden into chunky, greasy buds. Plants are vigorous and easy to read, stretching cleanly before settling into a steady swell, and they finish in roughly 8.5-9.5 weeks (about 59-67 days). Expect a loud nose where fresh orange rind and tangerine candy ride over a limonene-led terp profile, backed by grounding myrcene and a peppery caryophyllene twist. The palate follows through with sweet citrus and a light tropical echo, while the exhale hints at the Hash Burger lineage with faint earthy gas. Tropiburger was selected to move weight without babysitting, and it delivers: high yields, strong resin coverage, and eye-catching color that can wash from bright green to pink-lilac depending on phenotype. While potency will vary by selection, the cross is balanced and typically reads uplifting, happy, and relaxed without being racy. Bred and released by Nine Weeks Harvest, Tropiburger stands out as the practical workhorse of the drop that still carries a distinct, memorable identity. Growers can expect generous bag appeal and consistent performance across rooms.

name: Cobra Eye
description: Cobra Eye from Cipher Genetics splices the candied bite of Watermelon Warheadz with the exotic depth of Blue Lobster, producing a modern, indica-leaning hybrid bred for flavor, resin, and structure. Expect tall, vigorous plants with assertive lateral branching and tight internodes; flowers stack densely and finish under a silver glaze of trichomes within 60-65 days. Aromas lead with sweet watermelon candy and citrus before drifting into a creamy, gassy funk; on the palate it trends citrus-sweet with a tart edge. Caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool commonly steer the profile, underscoring a high-terp, extract-friendly finish. Effects arrive composed and uplifted, easing into a relaxed, euphoric cruise rather than a couch-locking thud. Indoor yields register medium while outdoor or dialed-in mixed-light runs can push high returns. Blue Lobster lineage hints at robust potency with trace CBD, while the Watermelon side adds playful, fruit-forward charm and lively clarity. Growers will appreciate the straightforward, easy cultivation, the tall stature that tops cleanly, and the bag appeal that holds after cure. For collectors chasing loud candy terps with a grown-up, funky backbeat, Cobra Eye hits the sweet spot, and gives due credit to its parents, Watermelon Warheadz and Blue Lobster. Released as a 7-pack feminized drop, it rewards simple training, thrives in controlled rooms, and turns heads from dry room to jar.

name: Banana Yuzu
description: Banana Yuzu by Bodhi Seeds marries the honeyed dessert notes of Honey Banana with the zesty, floral sparkle of Lavender Lemonaid. The bouquet opens with ripe citrus and lemon peel over soft lavender and fresh honey, while the palate leans creamy-sweet with tropical undertones and a faint pepper snap. Expect an indica-leaning hybrid structure: medium-tall plants with sturdy, lateral branching and a manageable stretch, stacking dense, sugar-dusted colas. Indoors, attentive training rewards growers with medium-to-high yields around 450 g/m2; outdoors, well-fed bushes can top 700 g per plant. Most phenotypes finish in 60–70 days, showing resin-forward flowers born for flavorful extracts. Typical potency falls between 20–26% THC with trace CBD (<1%), driven by a bright terpene ensemble of limonene, linalool, myrcene, and caryophyllene. The effect profile blends a cheerful, uplifted headspace with easygoing body calm, landing in that relaxed, happy middle ground that makes the cross shine without fogginess. Flavor lingers as honeyed honeyed citrus with a lavender glow on the exhale. Named for the aromatic yuzu fruit, Banana Yuzu captures Bodhi Seeds craft: a balanced, vivid hybrid that threads banana sweetness, lemon zest, and flowery charm into a single, memorable expression of its Honey Banana x Lavender Lemonaid lineage. Trichome coverage is generous, boosting bag appeal.

name: Doozy
description: Bodhi Seeds' Doozy is an aptly named mash-up of Milk Money and his Lavender Lemonaid, built for growers who crave bright lemon with a creamy twist. The nose sails from fresh lemon zest and lavender to sugared kush candy, and the flavor follows with sweet lemon, soft floral tones, and a faint creamy finish. Plants tend to stay medium in stature with sturdy laterals and tight, frosty colas, stacking well in tents. Indoors most phenotypes wrap in roughly nine weeks, keeping the workweek-friendly pace without skimping on resin. Expect medium yields and easy trim thanks to a favorable calyx-to-leaf ratio. The experience opens upbeat and happy, then coasts into a relaxed groove that never gets foggy. THC levels land squarely in the modern mid-to-high range, while CBD remains trace. Lavender Lemonaid supplies the lemon-linalool sparkle; Milk Money adds that powdered-sugar richness, making this cross feel both nostalgic and fresh. If your playlist swings from sunshine pop to smoked-out lounge, Doozy hits both notes, clean and indulgent, true to Bodhi Seeds' reputation for soulful, garden-ready selections. Bodhi credits the mama, Milk Money, for body and density, while the papa, Lavender Lemonaid, pushes citrus oil and linalool, a pairing that translates to sticky flower and bag appeal. Gardeners report cooperative feeding and moderate stretch, making canopy management straightforward with an uplifted overall tone.

name: Twin
description: Preferred Gardens' Twin pairs Zoap with a selected Lazer Gun cut to create a candy-gas hybrid with pedigree. Lazer Gun traces to Georgia Pie x Zkittlez, while Zoap descends from Rainbow Sherbet x Pink Guava, and that lineage shows in the jar. Twin opens with rainbow-candy and vanilla tones over assertive diesel and a faint rubbery snap; caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool lead the terpene trio, adding pepper, citrus, and floral lift. Recent batches clock around 26.3% THC with a whisper of CBD (~0.04%), delivering a relaxing, sedative calm that eases into happy, sleepy contentment without muddling focus. Frosted lime-and-mauve calyxes form dense, medium-sized nugs; break them and you'll catch candied guava and sherbet aromatics. In the garden, expect vigorous branching, manageable height, and a flowering window roughly 65-70 days; yields lean moderate when dialed in. Zoap's trophy pedigree (Best Overall, Zalympix 2022) peeks through in Twin's polished flavor and glossy resin, while Lazer Gun supplies the structured, gassy backbone PG fans recognize. Bred and released in-house by Preferred Gardens, Twin feels made for evening sessions when full-body ease and buoyant mood share the stage. Growers note moderate internodal spacing and a resin-forward canopy ideal for hash, especially in mixed-light and indoor rooms. High trichome density gives Twin a sugar-dusted finish and standout bag appeal.

name: Vodou
description: Vodou from Grandiflora Genetics channels the Oakland breeder’s flair for plush, high-octane hybrids. Its lineage reads like a modern hall of fame: Yadada blended with E85 and Doggy Bag. The result leans into a confectionary-gas profile—grape-candy sweetness riding over a firm ribbon of fuel—while earthy undertones linger on the exhale. Expect dense, resin-caked flowers with lime-to-deep-olive hues and amber pistils, a morphology that nods to both Cake and 4516. Reported effects tilt euphoric and happy before settling into an easy, body-forward calm, with classic hybrid composure rather than couch lock. Growers describe medium vigor and stature with cooperative internodes, rewarding attentive dialing with medium yields. Indoors, a 56–63 day finish suits dialed LED rooms; outdoors, late September to early October harvests are typical in temperate zones. Limonene and caryophyllene often headline, supported by myrcene, shaping the grape-diesel bouquet. Potency trends high for the category, commonly around the low-20s in THC with minimal CBD, so its flavor and intensity stand out without sacrificing clarity. However you encounter it—jar or garden—Vodou honors its parents while staking a confident place of its own, true to Grandiflora’s reputation for lush, high-terp expressions.

name: Fight Club
description: Fight Club by Lit Farms steps into the ring with serious pedigree, combining The Soap and Red Velvet into a slick, candy-tinged hybrid. Expect a burst of bright citrus and cool mint over creamy sweetness, a flavor arc that mirrors its aroma in the jar and on the exhale. Caryophyllene and limonene lead the terpene card with linalool in the undercard, shaping a profile that’s both zesty and polished. Indoors, plants keep a medium stature with hybrid branching and dense, frosted colas; they typically finish in about 56–63 days and return solid, medium yields with dialed-in light and airflow. Potency lands in the mid-20s THC in most cuts, with select phenos pushing toward the 30% mark, while CBD remains under 1%. The ride balances clear-headed focus with upbeat euphoria and a buoyant lift, an energetic throughline inherited from The Soap and rounded by Velvet Runtz’s confectionary calm. Released as a feminized offering under the Lit Farms banner (Lost In Translation), Fight Club has already proven its chops as a breeding piece, starring as the parent of Sucker Punch (/strains/sucker-punch) (Sucker Punch) (Fight Club x LIT OG). If you enjoy modern dessert-forward hybrids that still move with purpose, this polished brawler earns a spot in the lineup.

name: Rainbow Z by Backpakboyz
description: Rainbow Z by Backpack Boyz layers modern candy-gas genetics into a vivid, fruit-scented hybrid with serious depth. Built from Rainbow LCG crossed to Zkittlez, it blends creamy sherbet and sugary citrus aromatics with a grape-and-orange twist that lingers on the palate. Expect dense, trichome-frosted colas in shades of lime and plum with classic Z structure—chunky calyxes, wiry orange pistils, and a resin sheen that signals potency. The experience trends euphoric, happy, and tingly at first, resolving into a calm, relaxed cruise without losing its cheery, candy-forward character. Indoor gardeners can anticipate a medium-height plant with stout lateral branching and an 8–9 week bloom; yields are solid in the 450 g/m² range under dialed conditions, with outdoor plants finishing mid-season as compact, heavy clusters. As a packed flower drop from Backpack Boyz, Rainbow Z showcases the brand’s taste for confectionary profiles while keeping a smooth, refined burn. If you chase Z lineage done right, this cut delivers color, aroma, and a balanced, feel-good finish. Growers report moderate difficulty and best results with careful canopy management and steady, low-EC feeding.

name: Chanel
description: Chanel by Backpack Boyz pairs OZK with Gelato 41 to deliver a designer-level hybrid that looks and smells as curated as its name. In the garden, Chanel grows with medium vigor and an OG-leaning frame, stacking dense, frosted colas. Training for light penetration pays off. Flowering completes in roughly 60-70 days indoors; yields register in the medium range once dialed. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene commonly headline the terpene mix, reinforcing its sweet-citrus-earth trio. Backpack Boyz presents Chanel as a stylish intersection of candy-forward modern genetics and classic OG heft, built for fans of dessert aromas that still want a touch of fuel and structure. If you love OZK and Gelato 41, this cross lands squarely in that sweet spot.

name: Candy Float

Despite its craft pedigree, yields can run generously, especially indoors where canopies pack on weight without excessive height. Typical batches test around 15–20% THC with negligible CBD, delivering flavor-forward performance rather than a knockout. R.I.T.Z. contributes candy-gas sparkle and pace; Cherry Float adds creamy fruit and a calm landing, making Candy Float as comfortable in a creative afternoon as it is in laid-back conversation. Bred in collaboration with Hytek and released under the Pheno Addicts banner, this cut captures a modern candy-gas aesthetic while staying practical to grow and easy to appreciate. Expect medium height indoors and out, high yields with good canopy management, and resin-rich buds that press well.

Morphology is sturdy and cooperative, rewarding light training with symmetrical tops and glistening calyxes. True to its bakery namesake, Cherry Pavlova blends sweetness, balance, and polish — an inviting modern hybrid authored by G13 Labs and bred to deliver captivating aroma, resin-packed buds, and reliable performance for growers who want flavor without fuss.

name: Pistachio
