name: Raspado
description: Raspado is a hybrid cannabis strain developed by Jungle Boys, resulting from the cross between Sherb Cream Pie and Biscotti #15. This combination delivers a unique flavor profile and balanced effects. The aroma of Raspado is inviting, offering notes of tangy raspberry-lemon sherbet with a splash of gas up front and a smooth, doughy finish. Breaking open the buds reveals a more complex scent, adding layers of citrus zest and earthy sweetness. Flavor-wise, the strain presents a smooth blend of tangy raspberry-lemon sherbet with a doughy finish. Effects are calming and euphoric, making it suitable for evening use. Users often report a relaxed state with a gentle upliftin mood. It's ideal for unwinding after a long day. Medicinally, Raspado may assist with stress relief, mood enhancement, and promoting relaxation. Cultivating this strain is moderately easy, with an indoor flowering time of approximately 8–9 weeks. It thrives in stable environments with proper care.

name: D-Lish x Kamikaze
description: D-Lish x Kamikaze stitches candy-shop swagger to Z lineage finesse in a 50/50 hybrid selected and released by Preferred Gardens under The Gardens seed banner. One parent, D-Lish (Zkittlez × Sweet Retreat), brings the fruit-candy chorus that helped it podium at a major California terp showcase in 2025, while Kamikaze contributes the unmistakable depth of a prized Zkittlez cut. Expect a flood of fruity sweetness layered with bright citrus and soft vanilla cream, underpinned by a peppery-caryophyllene spine. Limonene, beta-caryophyllene, myrcene, and linalool typically headline the terpene stack, steering an experience that lifts mood and energy before settling into calm, buoyant equilibrium. Indoors, plants show stretchy, tall vigor with a tidy, lateral branch structure and frosted calyxes; flowering generally wraps in 56–63 days with medium yields that dial in around the mid-400 g/m² range when conditions are optimized. Potency commonly lands in the mid‑20s THC with trace CBD below 1%, expressed through dense, dusted flowers that flash lime-to-lilac hues and tangerine pistils. On the palate, the cross reads fruity, citrus, and sweet, with a syrupy Z backbone that lingers through the grind. Balanced yet assertive, this is a head-turner for candy-forward collectors and phenotype hunters alike.

name: Black Lily
description: Bred by Sensi Seeds Research for its 2026 lineup, Black Lily marries the loud, gassy punch of Adios MF with the cool, menthol-laced brightness of Vlad the Inhaler. This 65% sativa, 35% indica hybrid grows to a manageable 70–110 cm indoors and up to 2 m outdoors, stacking rock-hard, frost-caked buds that flash deep greens and purples. In the room it leans discreet only in stature—the bouquet swells from fizzy fuel and mint to sweet earth and kushy spice near harvest. Cured flowers carry a creamy, mint-forward inhale with diesel undertones and a lingering, earthy-spicy exhale. Classic sativa-leaning effects arrive first: an uplifting, focused wave and vivid euphoria, tapering gradually into a calm, body-centered glow that settles projects and evenings alike. Black Lily prefers structure: SCROG and mainlining shine; lollipopping and supercropping suit its sturdy branching; ultra-compact SOG runs are less ideal. Flowering completes in 70–75 days, rewarding patience with XXL harvests—about 460–650 g/m² indoors and roughly 550–750 g per plant outdoors—often requiring support for weighty laterals. With Adios MF's modern fuel character and White Label's Vlad the Inhaler (rooted in Chernobyl and Stoopid Fruits) supplying classic lineage, Black Lily balances contemporary flavor with proven vigor and yield.

name: Comfort Zone by Zaba Cannabis
description: Comfort Zone blends proven dessert and candy-gas lineages, pairing Seed Junky’s Sherb BX1 with Dying Breed Seeds’ OZ Kush. The result is a 75/25 indica-leaning hybrid that stacks chunky, resin-sheathed colas with lavender marbling and burnt-orange threads. Crack a jar and a swirl of vanilla-gelato cream and sweet citrus rides out first, quickly followed by peppery diesel and earthy OG undertones; on the palate it lands citrus-forward with a sugary lift and a clean fuel finish. Expect a buoyant onset that turns happy and unfussy before settling into deep, body-wide ease, the classic comfort zone vibe, with occasional dry mouth and eyes for some. Indoors, plants reach medium height with a cooperative, squat form; they respond well to light training and steady EC. Flowering wraps in roughly 56-65 days, rewarding dialed-in rooms with medium yields around 400 g/m2; sun-grown specimens can top about 700 g per plant in favorable climates. Dominant terpenes typically include beta-caryophyllene, limonene, humulene, and a linalool accent, echoing the strain's citrus-cream and gas identity. THC commonly lands in the low-to-mid 20s (observed parent range 15-30%), while CBD stays trace. Built from two contemporary pillars - Sherb BX1 and OZ Kush - Comfort Zone delivers modern bag appeal, candy-meets-fuel aromatics, and reliably serene, feel-good effects.

name: Magnum Runtz
description: Magnum Runtz from Lumpy's Flowers turns the cult-classic candy profile of Runtz into a bigger, brasher hybrid by pairing it with Gary Payton. Its dense, hand-trimmed buds stack with chunky calyxes and a heavy frosting of resin, flashing lime-to-forest greens with the occasional violet blush. Crack the jar and the room fills with sweet citrus candy over a peppery, gassy undercurrent; on the palate it layers bright lemon-lime taffy, soft cream, and a tickle of black pepper, a caryophyllene-forward bouquet supported by limonene and hints of myrcene. The onset is cheerful and clear, settling into a relaxed, contented body buzz without gluey heaviness, true to its balanced 50/50 heritage. Typical lots test in the mid-20s for THC (around 24% reported), with negligible CBD. In the garden, expect medium-height plants, moderate internodal spacing, and a cooperative temperament that rewards attentive feeding; indoor flowers usually finish in about 56-63 days with medium yields. Credit Lumpy's Flowers for refining the cross of Gary Payton x Runtz into a dialed-in production cut that preserves candy terp swagger while adding structure and gas. For connoisseurs chasing loud flavor and tidy, photogenic flower, Magnum Runtz hits the sweet spot between dessert-shop aroma and all-day usability. Balanced, bold, and unmistakably Lumpy's.

name: Strawberry Kōri
description: Strawberry Kori distills Raw Genetics' candy-forward breeding into a shimmering hybrid that makes its presence known the moment you crack the jar. Built from Zlushiez crossed to the flagship Zikigai, it leans hard into dessert terps: ripe strawberry syrup rides over sugared cream, tropical fruit punch, and a faint grapefruit snap that keeps the sweetness lively. In the garden it shows off why both parents are hashmaker favorites, stacking dense, resin-caked flowers from top cola to bottom with a crisp Z structure that washes well and cures with glossy frost. On the palate the profile stays laser-true - strawberry candy up front, rich Z fruit through the middle, and a clean creamy finish that lingers without heaviness. The experience opens with a bright, upbeat lift, nudging mood and chatter while keeping the head clear; as it settles, a smooth body calm spreads, leaving you relaxed, comfortable, and composed. THC expression varies by phenotype and grower technique, while CBD is typically minimal; what stays consistent is the strain's focus on aroma, flavor, and bag appeal. Bred by Raw Genetics and released under the Zikigai Garden banner, Strawberry Kori captures the modern "Z" ideal - louder fruit, thicker cream, and more output - wrapped in a beautifully frosted package.

name: Zabafibian
description: Zabafibian is Zaba Cannabis Co.'s amphibian-themed project built to bottle the minty gas and greasy resin that made Toad Venom famous. Anchored by a backcross to the Toad Venom cut, and by extension the Animal Face x Sin Mintz pedigree behind it, this selection delivers a loud, clean nose of diesel and cool mint over bright citrus and cookie-dough undertones. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene steer the terpene stack, translating to a palate that shifts from peppery fuel to frosted-mint candy with a lingering, OG-leaned finish. Plants tend to frame up medium in height with tight internodes and dense, trichome-soaked calyxes that drip into hash-friendly sugar leaves. In attentive rooms Zabafibian tracks an eight-to-nine week finish (roughly 56-63 days) and stacks solid, mid-column yields that can push toward half a kilo per square meter under dialed conditions. name: Acai and Bananas
description: Acai and Bananas is a delectable balanced hybrid created from a cross of Acaiberry Cake and Banana Punch and is known for its delicious tropical terpene profile and positive, happy high. As her name suggests, her flavor is a fruity blend of sweet banana and tropical acai berries, complemented by creamy vanilla notes and pungent earthy diesel. Her well-balanced effects start with an uplifted and creative head high with a bright cerebral buzz. A relaxing body high follows, delivering a lovely physical calm without crazy heavy sedation. She’s perfect for boosting mood and elevated creative sessions. As far as medical effects go, users could find Acai and Bananas helpful for soothing stress, anxiety, depression, chronic pain, and insomnia. She’s relatively easy to grow, with a flowering time of 56-63 days. Yield potential is high with optimal care, producing up to 500g/m2 indoors and as much as 600g/plant outdoors. Buds are dense and frosty, with minty light green buds with light purple hues, thin golden pistils, and a dense dusting shimmering, resin-rich trichomes.

name: Big E
description: Big E mixes West Coast icons into a lively, diesel-led hybrid that stays buoyant from grind to exhale. It's a tribute cross of Blue Dream and Sour Diesel, it later took first place in outdoor flower at Oregon’s inaugural Ganja Cup, and the lineage shows. Bright, petrol-laced top notes roll into earthy tones and a faint blueberry sweetness, driven by a terpene trio of myrcene, pinene, and caryophyllene. The effect profile skews sativa (about 70/30), delivering clear, creative lift and easy conversation alongside a gentle body buzz. Typical lab results land from roughly 17–24% THC with trace CBD up to about 1%, offering assertive potency without losing composure. In the garden Big E grows vigorously with lanky, sativa-style frames that like training and airflow; indoors or out, expect high yields of long, lime-green colas blanketed in frost. Flowering commonly wraps in 9–12 weeks (around 63–84 days), rewarding attentive growers with aromatic, resinous spears that trim quickly and cure into a sharp, skunky-diesel bouquet. If you are chasing the electric focus of Sour Diesel with Blue Dream’s fruit-kissed smoothness, Big E threads the needle and then some — an upbeat, social hybrid with pedigree and presence.

name: Gorilla Snacks
description: Heroes of The Farm's Gorilla Snacks blends the tenacity of Gorilla Glue #4 with Guinness, a Scooby Snacks F3 backcross, into a striking, resin-first hybrid. Expect medium-height plants that stack dense, sparkling colas and broadcast pungent pine layered with grape and subtle sweet-coffee undertones. Caryophyllene leads the terpene parade, with limonene and humulene close behind, shaping the strain's bold, gassy-woodland bouquet and a flavor that clings to the palate. Potency is serious: batches commonly land in the mid-20s, with THC reported between 20-32% and trace CBD up to ~1%. The high arrives in classic hybrid waves—an immediate lift that brightens mood and loosens conversation, then a calm, body-centered exhale-leaving most people relaxed, happy, and often a little giggly. Indoors, Gorilla Snacks is content under moderate training, finishing in 56-70 days and yielding around 500 g/m2; outdoors, expect medium stature, heavy trichome coverage, and up to roughly 700 g per plant where conditions allow. The cultivar's nickname nods to its appetizing, snack-worthy bouquet and the dense, gluey resin inherited from GG4.

name: Laura Palmer
description: Laura Palmer braids three cult classics into one modern hybrid, stitching the citrus-gas backbone of Paris Rock Candy (itself a Paris OG x Alien Rock Candy union) to the dessert-leaning charm of Marshmallowz ( Hollywood PK x MoonArc ), then electrifying the mix with Kiwi Sours from Alien Genetics. The result opens with a bright, candied nose — lemon and tropical fruit over sweet confection — before a deeper OG resin greets the exhale. Expect medium stature with strong lateral branching, dense calyx stacking, and a finish in roughly 56–60 days. Yields trend medium when run untrained, pushing higher with light canopy work. Dominant terpenes commonly lean toward limonene, linalool, and beta-caryophyllene, echoing the parents’ fruit, floral, and faint herbal-spice signatures. Potency sits comfortably in the mid‑20s THC with trace CBD, translating to a cheerful, euphoric lift that settles into contented calm without muting flavor. Kiwi Sours’ sour-candy snap adds definition, while the Marshmallowz line softens the edges into a creamy sweetness. For growers, Laura Palmer rewards stable environments and steady airflow around her chunky tops; for collectors, she reads like a love letter to Alien Genetics’ candy-forward lineage, with a polished finish that lingers long after the jar is closed.

name: Southern Sugar
description: Southern Sugar is an indulgent indica-leaning hybrid from Exotic Genetix that pairs Georgia Pie with Rainbow Chip, blending dessert-tier lineage into a modern crowd-pleaser. Its nose opens with vanilla and bright citrus overtones before tilting toward ripe peach candy; a faint pine-and-earth echo lingers on the exhale. Limonene, myrcene, and caryophyllene dominate the terpene stack, shaping a flavor that feels both creamy and zesty. Typical lab results place THC in the 20–25% window with low, trace CBD, while the effect profile skews upbeat and functional: a creative lift, calm focus, and gently euphoric mood that settles without heaviness. In the garden, Southern Sugar builds a medium‑tall, multi‑topped bush with symmetrical lateral branching and a high calyx‑to‑leaf ratio that cures into dense, frost-laden flowers worthy of its name. Indoors, plants stay compact; outdoors they reach a moderate stature. Expect a 56–63 day bloom and, under dialed conditions, reported harvests up to 700 g/m² inside and around 1,300 g per plant outdoors. Credit to Exotic Genetix for capturing Georgia Pie’s peachy sweetness and Rainbow Chip’s confectionary depth in a single, resin-rich hybrid that balances indulgent flavor with clear-headed composure.

name: Azul
description: Azul, also known as La Azul, blends the dessert creaminess of Sunset Sherbet with the decadent cookie funk of Biscotti, landing at a gently indica-leaning 60/40 profile. Its buds form dense, pepper-shaped clusters washed in forest green and deep blue, shot through with vivid orange hairs and a frosty coat of trichomes that glitters like powdered sugar. Crack a nug and a wave of sweet blueberry, spicy earth, and cool menthol rises, a sensory combo fans prize for both character and clarity. Reported THC typically spans the high teens to mid 20s (about 13-24%), while CBD stays minimal, setting the stage for a brisk, euphoric lift that spreads into a tingly, utterly relaxed body glow without heavy couchlock. Growers find Azul behaves like its pedigree: medium height, manageable branching, and medium-to-high yields when dialed in. Expect an indoor flowering window of roughly 60-70 days, with best expressions revealing sticky calyx stacks and that telltale blueberry-mint finish. Though specific terpene tests vary by cut, aromas often point to limonene, caryophyllene, and linalool steering the profile. Azul captures the shimmering, after-hours mood its name suggests: flavorful, striking in the jar, and satisfyingly balanced from first nose to last exhale.

name: Blue Dragon
description: Blue Dragon unites the sweet, old-school charm of Blueberry with the bright, gassy snap of Sour Diesel, delivering a hybrid that looks as bold as it smells. Often credited to Reefermans Seeds, this indica-leaning cultivar stacks dense, resin-frosted colas that can flash violet hues, with sturdy frames that finish in 8-9 weeks indoors. Expect a fragrant bouquet of ripe blueberry layered over citrus-tinged diesel and earthy undertones; on the palate those notes stay vivid and clean. Balanced potency is the rule here: lab reports commonly place THC around 18-24% with trace CBD (<1%), translating to a high that comes on euphoric and happy before settling into calm, body-light relaxation. Myrcene, caryophyllene, and limonene typically lead the terpene chorus, with pinene often in support, shaping its berry-diesel profile and uplifted mood. Growers with a bit of experience will find Blue Dragon cooperative: plants reach about 1.3 m indoors and up to 1.8 m outside, respond well to training, and reward attentive feeding with strong production. Indoors, yields near 450 g/m2 are achievable; outdoors, well-grown plants can return roughly 500 g each. In short, Blue Dragon blends West Coast swagger with classic flavors into a reliable, crowd-pleasing relaxed hybrid.

name: Grape Drink
description: True to its name, Grape Drink pours on confectionary purple notes from its parents, Kimbo Kush and Grape God, in a compact, indica‑leaning hybrid built for vivid flavor and plush resin. Expect dense, mint‑to‑violet buds dusted in trichomes and bright orange pistils, with an aroma that opens on grape and berry candy before drifting into sweet floral and citrus tones. Dominant terpenes myrcene, limonene, and beta‑caryophyllene steer the profile, complementing THC that typically ranges between 16–24% with trace CBD around 0–1% (often ~0.2%). The ride trends body‑forward and serene while keeping the head buoyant and social—relaxed, happy, and often a little giggly—making it as charming on the couch as it is with good company. Growers find Grape Drink straightforward: a small, bushy plant with tight internodes that finishes in about 56–63 days and rewards attentive light and airflow with solid yields. Indoors, expect roughly 400 g/m²; outdoors, around 550 g per plant when given warm, dry conditions.

name: Triangle Sherbet
description: Triangle Sherbet marries Florida’s legendary Triangle Kush with the dessert-forward Sunset Sherbet, delivering an indica-leaning hybrid that looks as frosted as it tastes. Expect medium-height, OG-shaped plants with a moderate stretch and dense, resin-caked colas that ripen in roughly 63 to 70 days. Its nose opens sweet and fruity with berry and citrus over an earthy, herbal undercurrent; on the palate, the profile tilts toward candied fruit and cream with a faint gas. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene typically drive the terpene ensemble, supporting a high that begins with an easy lift before settling into calm, body-centered relaxation and a quietly upbeat mood. Well-grown flower commonly tests in the mid-20s for THC, with standout phenotypes reported up to the high twenties, while CBD stays below 1%. Indoors, yields around 450–550 g/m2 are achievable with training, and cured buds show excellent bag appeal and extract-friendly resin. Bred from Triangle Kush x Sunset Sherbet, Triangle Sherbet captures the grit of Florida OG and the colorful sweetness of Sherbinski lineage in a single, cohesive expression.

name: Emerald OG
description: Emerald OG walks a steady line between coastal vigor and couch-friendly calm. Bred by the California Breeders Association, this indica-leaning hybrid unites Fire OG and Emerald Diesel, then was later backcrossed with Fire OG for extra OG heft. Aromas open with zesty citrus and sweet florals before settling into earthy pine; the palate mirrors that profile with a gentle vanilla echo on the exhale. Dense, bullet-shaped buds gleam bright emerald under a thick coat of trichomes and copper pistils. Typical THC spans 17–24% with CBD usually below 1%, while dominant terpenes—caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene—steer its character. The onset arrives clear and focused, easing into a deeply relaxed, sleepy finish that many enjoy in the evening. Indoors, plants tend to medium height and respond well to basic training, producing moderate yields in roughly 56–63 days of flower; outdoor gardens finish by mid-October in temperate climates. Fans describe plush body relief with a quietly uplifted headspace, aligning this cultivar with goals like unwinding after long days or easing racing thoughts. Growers note stout, conifer-like colas with minimal stretch.

name: Guava Berry
description: Guava Berry carries a bright tropical streak over an old-school backbone. Bred from Afghani and Chemdog, this slightly indica-leaning hybrid (about 60/40) blends a classic dense, resin-rich structure with a zestier, contemporary terpene profile. Aromas open with ripe berry and guava, pivot to citrus peel, then land on a gentle, spicy kush finish. The flavor tracks the nose: sweet-tart tropical fruit layered over faint earth and wood. Effects arrive quickly and lift the mood without fog: expect a clear, euphoric onset that sharpens focus and eases conversation before deepening into a more immersive, heady cruise. Potency typically sits around 18-20% THC with low CBD, offering presence without overwhelming heft. Growers see moderate vigor and a medium stature, with tight, rock-hard flowers and a favorable calyx-to-leaf ratio inherited from the Afghani side; yields are solidly moderate when dialed in. Indoors it behaves like many modern hybrids, finishing on a mid-cycle schedule under stable conditions. Buds show lime and forest greens threaded with amber pistils and a heavy dusting of trichomes.

name: Terpwin Station
description: Terpwin Station rides into the room on the shoulders of two modern classics, blending Original Glue and Mandarin Sunset in a terpene-forward hybrid from Ethos Genetics. Its structure leans tall and vigorous, stacking dense, resin-caked colas that echo GG4’s stickiness while flashing Mandarin Sunset’s citrus-tinted pistils. In the jar, sour orange and wildflower notes meet a whisper of sage and diesel; on the palate, expect a flowery-citrus sweetness with faint blueberry accents. Dominant terpenes often include caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene, and lab results from growers typically place THC between 15–25% with trace CBD below 1%. The experience arrives in stages: a clear, focused lift that sharpens creativity, then a deep, gluey calm that melts into the body and stokes appetite without muting mood. An indica-dominant 60/40 profile keeps effects balanced: relaxed yet mentally present, gently uplifting and reliably hunger-stirring. Growers report robust resistance and easy trimming thanks to firm calyxes and a low leaf-to-flower ratio. Indoors, plants commonly reach around 180 cm and finish in 60–70 days; with attentive training, yields are high both under lights and in the sun. Terpwin Station rewards dialed-in gardens with showpiece buds—frosted, lime-green, and loudly aromatic—true to its name.

name: Whipped Cherries
description: Whipped Cherries swirls classic dessert genetics into an indulgent, resin-rich hybrid. Bred by Exotic Genetix, it pairs Cherry Cream Pie with Cookies & Cream F2, a pedigree that comes through in the jar as sugared berry, cream, and soft vanilla over a faint nutty backdrop. Indoors the cultivar stays medium in stature with sturdy lateral branching and compact, golf-ball colas; it responds especially well to Sea of Green and light defoliation. Flowering finishes in 56-63 days, and dialed-in rooms can push yields from average into genuinely heavy territory. Buds are dense and often tip purple beneath a frosting of trichomes, reflecting an indica-leaning 70/30 profile. Typical batches test around 20-25% THC with minimal CBD, so expect a modern potency that still preserves flavor. The experience opens euphoric and happy before settling into a calm, relaxed body ease; many enthusiasts reach for it as a late-day unwind. Expect a flavor set led by berry and vanilla cream with a silky mouthfeel that lingers to the finish.

name: Mafiosa
description: Mafiosa from Obsidian Seeds blends two heavy-hitting parents, Horchata and M.O.B. , into a compact, flavor-driven hybrid with poise and punch. Expect the first break of the jar to push out sweet berry compote wrapped in creamy vanilla and a dusting of earthy spice - a profile that clearly nods to Horchata's gelato lineage while MOB layers in blueberry depth. Plants tend to stack dense, frosted colas on stout, well-branched frames, making training intuitive and trim time rewarding. In most rooms Mafiosa shows an indica-leaning posture with steady vigor and a quick, orderly finish: plan for roughly 7-9 weeks of bloom depending on phenotype, with solid mid-pack to generous yields when the environment is dialed. Caryophyllene and myrcene commonly lead the terp mix, with bright hints of limonene. Effects arrive in a smooth wave - relaxed and happy yet gently uplifted - suitable for winding down without shutting off creativity. THC expression varies by cut, while CBD is typically negligible, so potency feels modern without losing balance. The M.O.B. heritage brings a bit of East Coast lore (the Maine-born classic later placed second for Indica at ExpoGrow 2015 in Irun), and Horchata adds the dessert-like polish that gives Mafiosa its name.

name: Ztuntz
description: Named for its sugar-rush punch, Ztuntz a fuses two modern heavyweights into a vivid, candy-gas showcase. From the Runtz side come creamy gelato undertones and thick resin; from The Original Z (the cultivar once widely called Zkittlez) arrive layered fruit notes and that unmistakable "bag-of-sweets" nose. The aroma leads with sweet berry and tropical citrus over a peppery, gassy backbone, reflecting a caryophyllene-led terpene stack supported by limonene and myrcene, with linalool and humulene flickering between phenos. Expect a bright, uplifted start and easygoing happiness that settles into relaxed clarity, the classic Runtz/Z arc. Indoors, plants tend toward a medium-tall frame with vigorous lateral growth and dense, trichome-heavy flowers; topping and canopy control reward growers with fuller sites. Flowering typically wraps in 56-63 days, with medium-to-high yields under dialed conditions. Lab numbers vary by cut, but THC commonly lands in the mid-20s while CBD remains trace. Fans will recognize purple-to-lime calyx contrasts inherited from both parents. Outdoors it stretches modestly; indoors, tight internodes boost bag appeal. Most cuts finish frosty and vividly aromatic. Released by Global Genetics, this selection celebrates dessert-forward breeding without sacrificing gas, delivering a polished expression of two of the last decade's defining flavor lines.

name: Pink Zard

The experience starts upbeat and clear, with easy talk and a gentle head lift from the Red Hotz side, then glides into a calm, contented body ease as M.O.B. takes the wheel; overall, the vibe reads happy, euphoric, and relaxed. Plants stay medium in stature with sturdy laterals and tidy internodes; 60-70 days of bloom is typical, producing medium yields of eye-catching calyx piles. THC potential trends high while CBD remains low, and terpene expression commonly centers on limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene, reinforcing the candy-citrus-and-berry profile. Pink Zard hits a sweet spot between confectionary terps, color, and structure while carrying the unmistakable stamp of Obsidian Seeds.

name: Zhirley Temple

Crack the jar and the lineage jumps out: a bright lemon-lime splash and cherry-grenadine sweetness ride over strawberry, diesel, and a faint chemical tang. Caryophyllene leads the terpene trio here, with humulene and limonene rounding out the profile for a nose that is equal parts candy shop and gas station. On the palate it stays sugary and citric before a gassy finish. Reported effects unfurl in stages - first a buoyant, heady clarity, then a warm drip into the shoulders and limbs - eventually settling into a serene, heavy calm that many consider distinctly indica. Lab results commonly place potency around the mid-20s for THC (roughly 25%), with negligible CBD. Visually, Zhirley Temple often carries dense, frost-stacked buds with occasional violet flecks from Purple Punch and the cookie-style structure of Animal Cookies. While growers will not find a seed release, batches produced by Cresco tend to emphasize flavor saturation and a smooth, even burn rather than raciness. If you are hunting for a fruit-forward hybrid that still brings classic couch-friendly weight, this confectionery cross delivers the mocktail's cheerful sparkle wrapped in a decidedly stony finish.

name: Appalachia

Plants develop dense, frosty flowers with vibrant orange stigmas and a balanced, medium stature. Indoors, Appalachia finishes in about 56–70 days and delivers moderate yields; outdoors it ripens by early to mid-October in suitable climates. On the palate, sweet citrus and conifer evolve into a gassy, skunky finish, while the effect blends an upbeat, focused lift with a steadying body calm. Growers prize its manageable canopy, sturdy branching, and reliable trichome coverage that reflects both sides of its pedigree.

name: Grumpz

Outdoors, medium-height bushes finish by October with around 400 g per plant in good conditions. Grumpz's buds are long and fluffy with dark-lilac sugar leaves, amber crystal-leaning trichomes, and rusty pistils that hint at its dessert-heavy lineage. Fans prize its happy, relaxed, and euphoric vibe, while some note mild dryness or occasional paranoia at high doses. True to its pedigree, Grumpz marries Runtz's candy brightness with Grape Pie x MAC's rich, creamy grape overtones, creating a modern, photogenic cultivar that satisfies growers and connoisseurs alike. Expect dense, bag-appeal nuggets that trim easily and cure into a terp-loud jar.

name: Purple Goo

Most batches test in the mid-teens to low-20s for THC (roughly 16-22%) with trace CBD (~0-1%). Purple Goo's lineage shows in the finished buds: dense, frosted calyxes with the gooey stick of Afgoo and the regal color of Purple Kush. The original breeder remains unconfirmed, but seeds are sold as Purple Goo Feminized Seeds by Crop King Seeds. For fans of classic West Coast purples, this cross is a mood-smoothing nightcap with unmistakable grape-and-pine character and tidy, small-room-friendly stature.

name: Corked

She does stretch with healthy vigor but maintains a manageable form, rewarding growers who provide plenty of airflow and strategic trimming with resinous buds perfect for extractions. The palate is tangy and powerful, with high levels of limonene and myrcene playing a huge role in its tantalizing taste. Expect energetic and uplifting effects — delivering a clean, focused head high that boosts motivation and productivity. There’s just enough of a relaxed body buzz to keep you grounded rather than racy, but with zero sedation — making it a great daytime choice for both rec and medical users. name: Grandpa's Cookies
description: Grandpa’s Cookies by Ethos Genetics is a hybrid strain packing up to 18% THC, created as a cross between Grandpa’s Stash and Ethos Cookies. Packing reasonably balanced genetics, this praised cultivar also manages to blend skunky diesel notes with lemon and a faint sweetness that becomes more dominant in the aroma. The Grandpa’s Cookies high comes on fast, causing a tingly physical sensation and filling you with bliss and creative thoughts. An ideal strain for any time of day, know that it’s best enjoyed by experienced consumers. Medically, Grandpa’s Cookies is a great strain when dealing with anxiety, low mood, and chronic stress. The cultivation of these plants poses moderate challenges, especially regarding humidity levels that need to be spot on for optimal terpene production. They reach medium heights, flower for anywhere between 58 and 72 days, and are known to produce high yields, especially indoors.

name: Rainbow Punch
description: Rainbow Punch by Equilibrium Genetics is a heavily Indica-dominant hybrid strain resulting from a crossbreeding effort involving RS11 and Purple Punch, two equally sought-after cultivars. What we get from this promising communion is a flavorful variety boasting a profile dominated by citrus, fresh red grapes, and diesel. Rainbow Punch is a one-way ticket to happiness and relaxation, with the munchies, possible couch-lock, and a sleepy attitude being the most probable outcome. Medical patients suffering from insomnia, chronic stress, and hypertension are bound to benefit from this strain. Growing it requires insight and experience, as these plants are not the most forgiving. Prepare for aromatic ladies that demand odor control when grown indoors, follow a 9- to 10-week-long flowering cycle, and produce medium to medium yields between 350 and 450 g/m² when all conditions are met. They also reach medium heights and benefit from LST.

name: Sour Gorilla
description: Sour Gorilla, also known as Gorilla Diesel, is a Sativa-driven hybrid that’s also a celebrity child, coming forth out of the marriage between GG4 and Sour Diesel. Consumers are in for an uplifting cerebral energy rush, bringing creative ideas, a surge in focus, and a tingly sensation that slowly morphs into a more relaxed state of being towards the second half of the high. Medically, Sour Gorilla shines as an aid for patients seeking an alternative method to deal with depression, a chronic lack of energy, stress, and fibromyalgia. The Sour Gorilla flavor and aroma both blend diesel with ammonia and other chemical-like notes, making for a pungent and rather unique sensory experience. Cultivating these ladies is a guaranteed ticket to high yields, the need for strong odor control measures, and plants that are a joy to watch but require quite some ‘personal space’ for optimal results, as they can reach tall, even indoors.

name: Soul Mate
description: Soul Mate, a Bodhi Seeds creation combining the two in-house favorites Goji OG and Wookies, is one of those rare, evenly balanced hybrids that make a solid choice no matter the time of day. The flavor profile of this amazing cultivar is dominated by lemon, skunky notes, and strong lavender aromas, making for a memorable sensory experience. The Soul Mate high comes on fast with mellow and uplifting effects that put you in the best mood imaginable. Suited for both daytime and evening use, this strain is bound to please a whole range of consumers. Medically, Soul Mate should not be overlooked when dealing with depression, anxiety, and chronic stress. Growing these plants demands some experience. They reach medium heights, produce abundant resin, and are known to produce medium yields ranging up to 400 g/m². Indoors, they will probably demand odor control, and it’s important to cure the buds properly for optimal flavor and potency.

name: Hell On Wheels
description: Hell on Wheels, a hybrid strain created through a crossbreeding project involving 9 lb Hammer and Sunset MAC, is a product of Jinxproof Genetics that is sure to make an impression. When burned, the Hell on Wheels nugs release a sweet berry-driven flavor profile, infused with gas and hints of tangy lemon. The effects come on fast and strong, delivering a deeply relaxing high with long-lasting effects that almost always lead to drowsiness and couch-lock if left unchecked. Expect the feeling of not having a care in the world, creative ideas that slowly turn introspective, and the growing urge to take a nap or enjoy a good night’s sleep. Medically, Hell on Wheels should not be overlooked when dealing with chronic or acute stress, insomnia and other sleeping disorders, and pain. Cultivators are in for a rewarding and not overly challenging endeavor with these plants. They reach medium heights, stay rather bushy and manageable, and benefit from maximum airflow and light penetration if you want the 9 weeks of flowering to produce high yields.

name: Lemon Granita
description: Lemon Granita is a refreshing hybrid created from the bright and citrusy Lemon Jack and Frozen Margy genetics. This flavorful pairing resulted in a terpene-rich cultivar with manageable yet powerful THC levels that average 17-19%. This zesty lady known for her balanced effects bursts with bright lemony citrus aroma and flavor profile. She has a sharp lemon zest and sweet citrus candy flavor, and creamy undertones and subtle herbal and earthy notes on the finish. Prepare for an uplifting and clear-headed cerebral buzz that boosts mood, creativity, and focus. This happy head high is followed by a smooth and relaxed body buzz that never feels heavy or sedating. The balance makes her well suited for daytime or afternoon use. As far as medical effects, Lemon Granita is a good choice for users seeking relief from chronic fatigue, stress, anxiety, mild pain, and low mood. Growers will delight with her easy nature, making it a great choice for beginners and a rewarding for experienced cultivators. Plants are medium to tall, with a flowering time that usually wraps up in 56–67 days. Yields are rewarding with the right care, delivering dense, light to deep green hued buds, with bright orange pistils and a thick frosting of glistening trichomes.

name: Pink Diamonds
description: Pheno Addicts set out to bottle sparkle with Pink Diamonds, a cross of Yellow Diamonds and Pluto that blends citrus-bright lift with deep-space gas. The Pluto side lends dense, frosty flowers with a kush-forward backbone and occasional purple flashes, while Yellow Diamonds contributes a luminous trichome sheen and zesty, diesel-citrus aromatics. Expect a terpene profile led by limonene, myrcene, and caryophyllene, translating to flavors of sweet citrus over a faint fuel finish. On the nose it opens sharp and tangy before rounding into confectionary sweetness as the bud breaks. Effects arrive quickly and evenly: an uplifted, happy headspace pairs with a smooth, body-softening calm that settles into a relaxed groove without dulling focus. Growers can anticipate a medium-height hybrid with sturdy lateral branching, moderate internodal spacing, and a balanced stretch; it rewards consistent feeding and strong light with a medium yield of chunky, resin-heavy colas. THC potential runs high in this lineage, while CBD stays low, making Pink Diamonds shine where potency, bag appeal, and flavor converge. Bred and selected by Pheno Addicts, this cut captures the best of both parents in a polished, modern expression suited to connoisseurs and hash-makers alike. Expect a tidy indoor finish with balanced vigor and standout resin for solventless work.

name: Volonaut
description: Volonaut rockets out of the Pheno Addicts hangar, a Ducatti x Pluto cross built for flavor and frost. Ducatti (Biscotti x Bebesita Kush) contributes compact, dessert-leaning morphology and stout lateral branching, while Pluto (Gelato #33 x TK91 Bx1) layers in the dark, gassy depth that made the cut a cult favorite. Expect dense, resin-stacked flowers that can flash deep olive and occasional violet, with a nose that opens on diesel and berry, chased by a citrus twist. On the palate it tracks the jar: gas first, then sweet cream and blackberry rind. Typical dominant terpenes are myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene. The effect profile skews indica; users commonly report easy body calm, cozy drowsiness, and a serious case of the munchies. Indoors, Volonaut is at home in tight quarters, finishing in about 56-63 days; dialed rooms can return high indoor yields around 500 g/m2, while well-fed outdoor plants push toward 600 g per plant. Potency trends high-THC with low CBD, reflecting its modern dessert-cut pedigree. Growers should plan medium difficulty: vigorous veg, modest stretch, and tight internodes that reward good airflow. Credit to Pheno Addicts for a space-grade hybrid that feels both modern and timeless, equal parts creamy biscotti and out-of-orbit gas.

name: Venuz
description: Venuz channels the gleaming pop of modern exotics into a composed, heady hybrid born from Yellow Zushi and Pluto, selected and released by Pheno Addicts (Flavor Designer). Its aroma strikes first: bright citrus zest and tropical candy from the Zushi side riding over silky cream and a faint diesel twang, while Pluto deepens the bouquet with darker berry, pine, and OG spice. Expect dense, frost-caked colas with an indica-leaning frame, swollen calyxes, and occasional lilac highlights; inside, the terpene trio of limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and humulene carries through to a flavorful, lingering finish. The effect profile is confident yet composed-an uplifted, happy headspace coupled with steady body relaxation--ideal for slipping into creative focus without losing your equilibrium. Growers can anticipate a medium height and moderate vigor, stacking quickly in 56-70 days of flowering, with a solid medium yield when canopy and airflow are dialed in. THC commonly lands in the mid-20s, while CBD remains trace, emphasizing terpene expression and resin density. On the palate, Venuz leans citrus, tropical, and cream. On the feel, it stays balanced: clear, relaxed, and quietly euphoric. If you crave candy brightness with cosmic depth, this carefully curated Yellow Zushi x Pluto cross more than earns its celestial name.

name: Plulato
description: Pheno Addicts' Plulato stitches together the candy-coated charisma of Devine Runtz with the cosmic gas of Pluto, yielding a plush, indica-leaning hybrid tuned for modern flavor hunters. Expect a burst of citrus and tropical sweetness over creamy candy as the jar opens, then a deeper current of berry, pine, and light diesel when the grinder hits; on the palate, it stays sweet and lively with a smooth, gassy finish. Selected from parents known for glossy trichomes and dense, violet-flecked nugs, Plulato grows into medium-height bushes with stout lateral branching and resin-heavy colas. Dominant terpenes typically lean myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene, with pinene accents. Potency trends high: THC commonly lands in the mid–upper 20s with trace CBD below 1%. The ride starts upbeat and euphoric, brightening mood and focus before easing into a deeply relaxed, happy calm that lingers. Indoors, flowering usually wraps in about 56–65 days, and dialed-in rooms see medium yields that cure to a sugary, loud nose. Pluto's NorCal pedigree (Gelato #33 crossed to TK91 Bx1) contributes the skunky-citrus backbone; Devine Runtz layers tropical-candy sheen. Crafted by Pheno Addicts, Plulato reads like a connoisseur's dessert hybrid—clean structure, confident potency, and a flavor arc that stays sweet without sacrificing depth.

name: Pineapple Pluto
description: Pineapple Pluto from Pheno Addicts fuses the sun-splashed zest of Pineapple Mambaz with the brooding, purple-leaning power of Pluto, yielding an indica-leaning hybrid that smells like a fresh-cut pineapple over creamy tropical candy and faint kush-fuel. In the jar, notes of mango, citrus peel, and sweet berry announce a myrcene- and limonene-forward profile with peppery caryophyllene lurking underneath; ground flower tilts gassy while the exhale stays bright and sugary. Structure reflects its lineage: squat, tidy branching, tight internodes, and chunky, trichome-caked colas that can blush violet late, a visual nod to its Pluto parent. Indoors it prefers moderate feed and airflow, stacking best in a short veg, and typically finishes in 56–65 days of bloom. Expect medium yields of resinous buds with excellent bag appeal. The ride balances uplifted, giggly headspace with a calm, body-centered ease, settling into a serene, contented focus rather than couchlock. Trace CBD and robust THC potential make the cut feel modern and expressive without losing the classic kush backbone. If your palate leans toward tropical desserts with a diesel ribbon, Pineapple Pluto delivers a polished take on that lane—credit to Pheno Addicts for a cross that captures pineapple brightness and planetary depth in equal measure.

name: Blue Pluto
description: Blue Pluto blends Pheno Addicts' dessert-forward Blue Ritz with the GasHouse-popular Pluto cut to create a modern hybrid that shows dense, resin-rich flowers and expressive terpene intensity. Expect blueberry and cream-soda aromatics from the Blue Ritz side, trimmed by Pluto's citrus zest and faint diesel-earth undertones for a sweet-then-bright finish. Plants generally stay medium in stature with compact internodes, rewarding basic canopy work with tidy structure and moderate yields. Indoors, most phenotypes finish in about 56–63 days; cool nights late in bloom can tease out violet flecks beneath a thick frost. In the jar, buds present as sugar-dusted golf balls with orange pistils and occasional purple hues. The flavor follows the nose—blueberry candy, cream, and citrus—while effects tend to open with a buoyant, euphoric lift and settle into a calm, contented relaxation without heavy couchlock.

name: Zkrilla
description: Zkrilla blends the muscled indica drive of Godzilla with the candy-gas finesse of R.I.T.Z in a polished release from Pheno Addicts under the Flavors Designer banner. The nose fires first: bright citrus and orange peel laced with pepper and soft florals, the carryover on taste shot through with a faint diesel ribbon and a gentle vanilla creaminess. That profile reads squarely limonene and caryophyllene with linalool in support. Effects rise smoothly into an easy euphoria and buoyant uplift before settling into an even, loosened calm, the kind that unties the jaw and brightens the mood without fog; most report a relaxed, upbeat cruise rather than a knockout. Plants stay compact and calyx-forward, stacking dense, frosted flowers that finish in roughly 56–63 days indoors. Expect medium yields with tidy trim work and a cooperative, medium-difficulty cultivation curve. Structure leans short to mid-height with good internodal spacing; dialed lighting and airflow reward resin and color. No surprise given the pedigree: Godzilla lends stout frame and staying power while R.I.T.Z contributes the confectionery-fuel shine and bag appeal. Zkrilla is a smart pick for growers chasing citrus-forward candy with modern gas in an indica-leaning frame, credibly sourced and curated by Pheno Addicts.

name: Blue Caviar by Hall of Flame
description: Blue Caviar brings connoisseur swagger to the jar, pairing Blue Zushi with Gushers BX in a boutique cross by Hall of Flame. Blue Zushi, the celebrated Zkittlez x Kush Mints cut popularized by The Ten Co. and crowned at the 2023 California Zalympix, donates its candy-mint bouquet and thick frost. Gushers BX, a backcross of the Gelato #41 x Triangle Kush line, layers extra gas and syrupy fruit. Expect dense, sugar-dusted nugs and an aroma that opens with berry and bright citrus before cooling to mint, sweet dough, and a faint diesel echo. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene lead the terpene chorus. Reported effects skew upbeat and relaxed: a mood-lifting, euphoric lift that eases into a calm, clear focus without heaviness. Indoors the medium-stature plants stack tight calyxes on sturdy laterals, finishing in 56-68 days with high yields around 450-550 g/m2; outdoors, well-grown plants can push roughly 900 g per plant. Potency lands in the 20-28% THC window with sub-1% CBD. If you chase Blue Zushi's trophy terp profile but want deeper candy-gas from the Gushers line, Blu Caviar distills both into one polished, photogenic hybrid that rewards careful dialing of light, temperature, and airflow from flip through the fade to finish.

name: Devine Runtz
description: Devine Runtz steps out of the Runtz family as a candy-forward showcase of Gelato 33 x Zkittlez. A true 50/50 hybrid, it routinely tests at 24-27% THC with about 1% CBD, pairing quick, euphoric lift and bright, happy chatter with an even, body-softening calm. The bouquet is sweet and tropical with citrus peel sparkle; flavors echo that fruit-candy core while pinene adds a crisp pine note and beta-caryophyllene a gentle pepper warmth over myrcene's soft earth. Compact, resin-frosted spears can flash deep purples beneath vibrant orange pistils, and plants remain medium in stature (roughly 5-8 feet) when untrained. Indoors, expect 56-63 days of bloom and around 400-600 g/m2; outdoors, medium yields near 400-450 g per plant, with harvests landing in mid-October. Growers report accessible, medium difficulty and responsive structure that rewards canopy control and steady humidity. Typical positives include euphoria, happiness, and relaxation; occasional dry mouth, dry eyes, or dizziness may appear. Whether hunted as a standout pheno or offered as a stabilized seed line, Devine Runtz captures what made its parents modern icons: dessert-like flavor, glossy trichomes, and a steady, feel-good cruise from first aroma to last exhale. Under temperate, sunny conditions, plants average roughly 198 cm when given room, maintain medium stature indoors and out, and respond well to topping or low-stress training for even light.

name: Golden State Banana
description: Golden State Banana is an indica-dominant hybrid (about 70% indica, 30% sativa) created by Nick Bryan's Golden State Banana brand from Ghost OG and Banana Kush. Its bright, banana-forward bouquet folds into citrus and tropical tones over an earthy, pungent base, a profile driven by myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene. Expect dense, bullet-shaped buds lacquered in frost, a medium stature (roughly 80–140 cm) with strong, upright growth, and wide internodal spacing that fills quickly in bloom. Indoors it typically finishes in 49–63 days and, under dialed conditions, returns around 450–600 g/m2; outdoors, well-grown plants can top 500–700 g apiece. Potency is formidable: batches often test in the mid-20s, with verified ranges near 23–30% THC and trace CBD. The experience opens with a smooth wave of euphoria and uplift before settling into a deep, contented body calm; tingly, sleepy edges are common late in the arc, yet the mood stays warm and happy. Fans prize its steady, indulgent flavor — ripe banana, citrus peel, tropical candy — without overwhelming skunkiness. Growers note moderate difficulty: keep airflow strong and humidity in check to preserve resin and that signature dessert terp stack. Golden State Banana remains a West Coast favorite that marries OG structure with sun-sweet fruit.

name: Apple Cider
description: Apple Cider blends a prized Apple Fritter (Lumpy's Cut) with the loud, resinous Pure Michigan, a union first released by Green Wolf Genetics. This indica-leaning hybrid grows medium in stature with sturdy lateral branching and dense, golf-ball flowers that frost over early. In the jar it reads like its name: crisp apple up front with honeyed sweetness and a soft ribbon of vanilla over earthy, nutty undertones; caryophyllene leads the terpene chorus with supporting hits of limonene and myrcene. Potency lands in the 15-24% THC window with trace CBD around 0.2%, delivering a euphoric, creative lift that settles into calm, body-forward relaxation. Indoors, Apple Cider typically finishes in 8-10 weeks (many phenos wrap in roughly 56 days) and rewards dialed gardens with about 400-500 g/m2; outdoor plants, medium in height, commonly return 500-600 g per plant by early October. Morphology shows a moderate 1.3-1.6x stretch at flip and a tidy, dome-shaped canopy that is easy to manage. While the Apple Cider moniker is new, its pedigree carries history: Apple Fritter famously hit High Times lists and podiums in 2016, and Pure Michigan contributes the dark, resin-stacking vigor breeders prize.

name: Bubble Spritz
description: Bubble Spritz channels the candy-shop lineage of Seed Junky Genetics into an indica-dominant hybrid that balances charm and horsepower. Bred by Seed Junky from Bubblegum Sherb and Biscotti x Sherb BX, it leans 70/30 indica/sativa and typically tests around 19–22% THC. Expect stacked, dense flowers glazed in trichomes, with a terpene bouquet led by caryophyllene and rounded by limonene and myrcene. The nose pops with sweet berries, classic bubblegum, and a whisper of earth; the flavor follows suit, finishing clean and sugary. The experience tends to start bright and social, drifting from talkative ease into a relaxed, sleepy coast as the session unfolds. Growers appreciate straightforward, vigorous growth and a medium stature that responds well to simple training. Indoors, bloom wraps in nine to ten weeks and well run rooms can return up to about 700 g/m2; outdoors, individual plants have been recorded near 1.25 kg in favorable climates. Created under the Seed Junky banner, Bubble Spritz lifts the boutique dessert profile of its parents and packages it with modern bag appeal and reliable structure.

name: Snake Venom
description: Snake Venom coils its heritage from Moxie 710 into a stealthy, indica-leaning hybrid that snaps to life the moment it flowers. Born from Viper City and Gorilla Glue #4, its clustered colas develop from 120–150 cm plants into gleaming, resin-glazed buds that finish in 50–60 days. Citrus-diesel terpenes lead the nose—lemon, skunk, and fumes of fuel—while the palate echoes with creamy lemon-diesel and a hint of pine. Typical lots test around 20–24% THC with negligible CBD, and yields can be generous: experienced hands regularly pull 500–600 g/m² indoors. The effect sneaks in, then washes over with a tingly body calm and heavy relaxation before drowsy contentment settles; fans prize the strain for its deeply unwinding, end-of-day demeanor without sacrificing a quietly lifted mood. Colors range from deep olive to pearlescent purples, dusted by thick white frost that betrays its Gorilla lineage. Moxie 710’s selection emphasizes a medium stature and high production balanced by demanding cultivation, rewarding attentive dialing of feed, airflow, and trellising. If your garden favors compact, high-output plants with skunky-citrus personality and a couch-friendly finish, Snake Venom’s bite is as memorable as its name, and its pedigree explains why.

name: Tomahawk
description: Tomahawk by Greenpoint Seeds flies straight from the Chem/Glue bloodline, pairing Josey Whales’ Gorilla Glue #4 with Greenpoint’s proven Stardawg male. In the garden it grows medium to tall, with long, sturdy branches and heavily frosted colas that finish in about 9–11 weeks. Yields are generous—around 400 g/m² indoors and roughly 400 g per plant outdoors when dialed—making it as practical as it is pretty. Open the jar and you get a punchy bouquet of skunk and diesel layered over earthy coffee and a hint of pine; the flavor echoes that profile with a lingering, savory finish. Potency lands in the low 20s, typically 22–23% THC, balanced by a trace of CBD near 0.7%. The high starts with an upbeat, euphoric lift and clear, uplifted headspace before settling into a calm, gluey relaxation that speaks to its lineage. Caryophyllene, myrcene, limonene, and pinene commonly headline the terpene ensemble. True to its parents—GG4’s award-winning resin and Stardawg’s vigor—Tomahawk is hardy, beginner-friendly, and responds well to training.

name: Gelato High Octane
description: Gelato High Octane fuses dessert-tier Gelato with the horsepower of High Octane OG, yielding dense, round buds in olive green with vivid orange pistils and a frosty mantle of white trichomes. The scent opens with sweet citrus and pine before shifting to diesel and berry; on the palate it stays spicy-fruity with a clean, herbal fuel finish. Dominant terpenes caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene steer both flavor and feel, supporting an indica-leaning profile near 70/30 that typically tests around 25% THC with about 1% CBD. Expect a bright, social lift that eases into relaxed, happy euphoria without heavy lock. Growers find it compact indoors (roughly 0-4 ft) and medium outdoors (5-8 ft), finishing in 8-9 weeks, or about 56-63 days. Yields run boutique-low under lights (around 56 g/m2) but can swell outdoors to roughly 560 g per plant in tuned conditions. Bred from Gelato (Sunset Sherbert x Thin Mint GSC) crossed to High Octane OG, this cultivar threads confectionery gelato tones through classic OG gas.

name: Sour Blue Sunrise
description: Sour Blue Sunrise greets the day with a sativa-leaning glow, a cross of Blue Sunset Sherbet and Sour Tangie from Tahoe breeder Ross Miller. Dense, jewel-toned buds swirl greens and purples with near-blue flecks, set off by vivid orange hairs and a dusting of golden trichomes. Cracking a jar releases blueberry-pie sweetness over vanilla cream, quickly chased by tart, sour accents and a faint diesel edge; on the palate, blueberry, diesel and vanilla lead the chorus while lighter citrus notes hum beneath. Its dominant terpenes – terpinolene, pinene, and ocimene – steer the profile toward bright, zesty aromatics and a lively headspace. With THC around 22%, effects tend to lift and energize, nudging creativity and good humor while keeping the body light and mobile. Growers note it prefers indoor rooms where its sturdy frame stays manageable through veg, rewarding attentive dialing with a colorful, resin-forward finish. Expect a sativa-forward hybrid expression from its lineage: Sour Tangie contributes speed and citrus snap, while Blue Sunset Sherbet layers confectionary depth and bag appeal. Whether hunted for terp brilliance or its striking, sunrise-hued flowers, Sour Blue Sunrise delivers a crisp, modern take on a classic fruit-and-fuel family tree. Low CBD and a resilient growth habit round out the profile, making this cultivar a photogenic, terp-driven standout in curated collections.

name: Pootie Tang
description: Colorado-bred and cup-tested, Pootie Tang brings zesty drive and Kush backbone to the garden and the jar. Bred by New House Seed Co from LA Kush and Tang Tang, this sativa-leaning hybrid (about 70/30) marries bright citrus, grapefruit, and earthy-pine tones with a peppery finish. Limonene and terpinolene do the heavy lifting on aroma, with caryophyllene rounding out a subtly herbal bite. Expect an uplift that lands fast and sparkly, sharpening focus and mood before settling into a light, comfortable body buzz. THC commonly ranges 16-26% with trace CBD around 0-1%. Plants stretch vigorously with upright, branching architecture and foxtail-prone colas dusted in snowy trichomes and orange pistils. Indoors, a skilled hand can pull roughly 400 g/m2 in 59-73 days of bloom; outdoors, single plants often tip past 500 g by early to mid-October in temperate zones. Pootie Tang responds well to topping, LST, and a strategic day-21 defoliation to improve airflow and even canopy light. Resin production makes it a solid choice for solventless work. On the scene since 2012, this cultivar earned third place for Best Colorado Sativa Flower at the High Times U.S. Cannabis Cup in Denver in 2015, a nod to its lively, clean expression that still carries a touch of classic LA Kush hashiness.

name: Hitman OG
description: Hitman OG is DNA Genetics Seeds limited-edition OG that lives up to its name. An indica-dominant hybrid (about 80/20), it descends from OG Kush crossed to an undisclosed indica-leaning partner, preserving the classic fuel-and-pine profile while adding extra weight and resin. Dense lime-green spears stack along sturdy branches, flashing thick amber frost as plants stretch early and finish in 56-63 days. Growers report vigorous, tall morphology that responds well to trellising; yields land impressively around 450-550 g/m2 indoors. Terpene expression leans on myrcene with bright limonene and crisp pinene, translating to zesty lemon, conifer sap, and a diesel undercurrent. Potency is unapologetic: lab results and grow reports commonly place THC in the 20-29% window, with only trace CBD. The experience opens with a clean uplift before settling into deep body calm and heavy-lidded ease, true to the OG family's reputation. Bred by DNA Genetics Seeds as a short-run project, Hitman OG became a sought-after jar filler and a reliable parent in boutique crosses thanks to its combination of gassy flavor, big-bud OG structure, and straightforward cultivation. If you are after a modern, high-octane OG that still finishes fast and stacks hard, Hitman OG delivers. Its pedigree traces to OG Kush x an Unknown Strain, with an indica share near 80%.

name: MAC Cake
description: Mac Cake marries MAC with Wedding Cake into an indulgent hybrid that looks and smells like dessert. This indica-leaning cultivar stacks dense, frosted calyxes that glint like sugar under light. Crack a jar and you are greeted by vanilla icing and sweet cream over an earthy, diesel edge; the bouquet carries through on the palate with a smooth, cakey finish. Plants stay medium in stature, typically 80-140 cm indoors, and flower in 8-9 weeks (about 56-63 days). With straightforward, intermediate-level cultivation, Mac Cake reliably returns 450-600 g/m2 under dialed conditions and can push even higher with strong light and training. Tests and vendor data commonly place THC between 22-26% with trace CBD around 0.1-0.5%, translating to a vivid, uplifting onset that settles into a calm, contented body glow. The overall experience trends happy, relaxed, and gently euphoric without losing clarity. Expect standout bag appeal thanks to heavy trichome coverage and contrasting orange pistils, plus a modern dessert-gas aroma that plays well in rosin and other extracts. If you are searching for a contemporary crowd-pleaser built on proven parents, Mac Cake delivers the celebration. Growers note a balanced, medium height and short internodes that encourage stacked colas and make canopy management simple across phenos.

name: Popcorn
description: Popcorn from Lupos CannaSeed pops with a flavor arc that mirrors its lineage: Apple Pie Moonshine (Apple Fritter x Something Special) meets Bonkers (Lemon Tree x Cookies & Cream F2). Expect bright lemon zest and soft vanilla cream riding over sweet, pastry-like undertones, a profile driven by limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene. The hybrid effect lifts first - clear, upbeat, and creative - before easing into a comfortable body calm that leaves the mood buoyant rather than drowsy. Plants show stacked, popcorn-shaped colas and a dense, shimmering trichome jacket, with medium height and a cooperative, branchy structure that takes well to topping, LST, or a light scrog. Indoors, flowering wraps in roughly 65 days; greenhouse and outdoor runs finish on a similar clock in temperate climates. Yields land in the medium range with consistent feed and strong light, and the release is feminized-only for straightforward selection. While lab results vary by batch, Popcorn tends to express elevated THC with trace CBD, translating the dessert-meets-citrus family tree into a bright, modern hybrid you can recognize by its crisp lemon, confectionery sweetness, and silky cream finish. Expect medium internodes, quick stacking, and easy trim thanks to tight calyx formation. A tidy, adaptable cultivar authored by Lupos CannaSeed, it balances aroma, resin, and poise in equal measure.

name: MAC 4
description: Miracle Alien Cookies in a focused direction, showcasing a selected phenotype of Capulator’s cross of Alien Cookies × (Colombian × Starfighter). Expect compact, resin‑plastered flowers with a medium stretch and a tidy, branchy form that tops out at a manageable indoor height. The nose blends blueberry and berry sweetness with a diesel thread; caryophyllene leads the terpene chorus, supported by myrcene and pinene, for a sweet‑spicy profile that lingers. Reported effects lean clean and upbeat — focused, energetic, and uplifted — before easing into calm balance, a vibe that made MAC phenos favorites on connoisseur shelves and even fixtures in competition lineups. Typical potency lands in the low 20s, with MAC #4 often hovering near 22% THC and trace CBD, delivering clarity without heaviness. In the garden, MAC #4 prefers attentive dialing: moderate feeding, strong airflow, and patience through a 60–66 day bloom reward cultivators with frosted colas and moderate‑to‑heavy yields. Whether you know MAC for its glacial trichome coverage or for its hybrid poise, MAC #4 preserves the line’s hallmark flavor, sheen, and snap while sharpening its bright, fruit‑diesel personality.

name: Blue Mints
description: Blue Mints threads a cool sweetness through every stage of the grow and the grind. Bred by Sin City Seeds from SinMint Cookies and Blue Power, this indica-leaning hybrid shows off colorful, frosted colas that finish in greens and violets with bright orange pistils and heavy resin. Aromas skew toward berry-and-cream with an icy mint snap, while the flavor lands like a blue-raspberry slushie layered with sweet blueberry, faint cheese, and a clean herbal finish. Limonene and caryophyllene sparkle in the bouquet, but myrcene leads the terpene chorus, shaping the strain’s rounded profile. Expect a mood-lifting onset that soon settles into a calm, happy glow and gentle euphoria; most batches test around 28% THC with trace CBD near 0.45%. Growers can anticipate medium-height plants, a moderate-to-high yield, and an 8–9 week flowering window, making Blue Mints a tidy, predictable performer in dialed-in rooms. Structure is sturdy with cookie-dense buds that trim clean and cure to a silver sheen. Blue Mints distills the dessert charisma of its parents into a versatile, modern hybrid that looks boutique, smells nostalgic, and smokes with satisfying clarity. Gardeners appreciate its cooperative, cookie-leaning structure.

name: Pre Nup
description: Pre Nup marries dessert and space fuel in a lively, sativa-leaning hybrid from 1904 Genetics, created by crossing Wedding Cake with (GG4 x Triangle Mints Bx1) cross. Expect medium-stature plants with a sturdy central stem and studded laterals that set dense, frost-silvered colas; cured buds show deep emerald with occasional violet flecks. The bouquet is bright and piney up front, layered with sugary citrus-lime and a gentle vanilla sweetness, while the flavor tracks citrus, pine, and sweet bakery notes. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene typically steer its terpene profile. Potency lands in a versatile window, with THC commonly 15-23% and CBD around 0.2-0.4%. The experience leans upbeat and clear: an immediate lift into happy, euphoric focus that can feel lightly tingly before settling into calm composure. Indoors, Pre Nup finishes in 56-63 days; trained canopies reward with about 400 g/m2, and outdoor plants average near 400 g per plant. Its moderate internodes, good branch strength, and cooperative feeding make it an approachable, low-maintenance grow, especially where medium heights are preferred.

name: Honeydew Boba
description: Honeydew Boba is a sativa-leaning hybrid that tastes as playful as its name suggests, blending honeyed melon, bright citrus, and soft apricot spice. Built from celebrated parents Super Silver Haze and Appalachia (Green Crack x Tres Dawg), it carries the former’s classic, uplifting haze character and the latter’s fruity, skunky backbone. Most cuts test around 19–21% THC with trace-to-1% CBD, though top-shelf batches have reached the low 30s. Expect a quick cerebral lift that feels energetic, happy, and distinctly upbeat, with a clear, chatty edge before settling into a breezy, functional cruise. The nose is sweet and tropical with floral undertones; myrcene often leads the terpene mix alongside limonene and caryophyllene. Plants stay compact indoors (roughly 0–4 ft) and medium outdoors (5–8 ft). Flowering wraps in about 56–63 days, and attentive growers can pull high yields; indoor rooms reward dialed-in training and light management, while outdoor sites finish near early October. Buds show lime-green hues with a frosty sheen and easy bag appeal.

name: Silver Pearl
description: Silver Pearl sparkles with old-school pedigree and modern utility. Bred by Sensi Seeds in the early 1990s, this sativa-leaning hybrid stitches together Early Pearl and Skunk #1, then layers in Northern Lights #5 to compact the frame and drench the flowers in resin. Expect medium-height plants with a high calyx-to-leaf ratio, spear-shaped colas, and a quick finish - most gardens see full bloom in 49-63 days. Aromas mingle bright citrus and honey over a skunky baseline; the flavor tracks the nose, tilting toward citrus zest, honeyed sweetness, and classic skunk. Typical lab panels place THC around 13-21% with CBD commonly under 1%. Myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene often lead the terpene profile, supporting an upbeat, euphoric lift that stays clear, creative, and pleasantly uplifting. Indoors, dialed canopies return about 400 g/m2; outside, sturdy, mid-sized bushes can yield roughly 550 g per plant under favorable conditions. Silver Pearl's shimmering trichome coverage and straightforward growth made it a coffeeshop staple and earned it accolades at the 1994 High Times Cannabis Cup. For growers who crave fast, sparkly sativa energy without unruly stretch, Silver Pearl delivers a bright, classic profile in a compact, cooperative package that honors its three cornerstone parents. Expect vigorous rooting, easy trim work, and glistening, sugar-dusted buds.

name: Cake Frosting
description: Cake Frosting by Moksha Seed Co layers forest-sweet aroma over a fast finish, true to its parents The Sauce #1 and Drive Thru Wedding #3. The bouquet opens with sweet pastry and damp-earth notes before a clean pine uplift, echoing a rainy-woods stroll, with a pinene-led terpene mix backed by caryophyllene and myrcene. On the palate, soft sugar and cake crust meet lime-diesel flecks from The Sauce, while Drive Thru Wedding lends a creamy, cookie-spiced undertone. Plants grow in a classic Christmas-tree shape with strong, well-braced laterals, responding eagerly to topping and stacking broad, colorful colas. Indoors they stay medium in stature and wrap up around 63 days, often flashing frosty calyxes that hint at THC-forward potency with only trace CBD. Expect a balanced, mood-lifting head that settles into relaxed clarity; typical reports emphasize happy, uplifted calm with focus intact rather than couchlock. A nod to lineage: The Sauce from Exotic Genetix earned a judges choice at a Seattle cup, and that pedigree shows here as resin sheen and vivid flavor density. Growers describe yields in the medium-to-high range when light and airflow are dialed, with sturdy branches that carry weight without sag. Cake Frosting delivers its name honestly: aromatic sweetness, forest earth, and a cool pine finish, all neatly iced in trichomes.

name: Citrus Berry
description: Exotic Genetix’s Citrus Berry marries the candy-coated punch of Kimbo Kush with the zesty drive of Orange Valley OG, and the result lives up to its name. Dense, triangular flowers flash lime and deep violet under a heavy frost, while the room fills with mixed berries, sweet citrus, and a hint of sour cherry and kushy spice. A terpenoid profile led by terpinolene with support from limonene, myrcene, and caryophyllene translates to bright, fruity top notes over earthy kush. Most batches test in the mid to upper teens through low 20s for THC (roughly 15–23%) with trace CBD around 0.03%, shaping a gently uplifting onset that settles into a soothing, full-body calm and, for many phenos, drowsy finish. In the garden, this slightly indica-leaning hybrid stays medium in stature and responds well to topping, rewarding dialed-in rooms with high yields of sticky, resinous buds. Expect an indoor flowering window of about 56–63 days and consistent performance both indoors and out. Though now retired from the catalog, Citrus Berry endures among collectors for its pastry-sweet flavor, friendly hybrid demeanor, and bagside appeal that pops as soon as you crack the jar.

name: Truffle Sundae
description: Like a dessert served after dusk, Truffle Sundae arrives with the cocoa-tinged depth of Chocolate Kush and the creamy, candy lift of Gelato 41. This even 50/50 hybrid layers vanilla-sweet aromas over an earthy, faintly pungent base; crack the dense, frosted nugs and you may catch hints of caramel and coffee alongside gelato-like fruit. Typical batches test 18–24% THC with about 0.45% CBD, and the terpene trio of myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene steers the profile toward confection and spice. In the garden it keeps a tidy frame indoors (roughly 0–4 ft), stretching moderately under bloom and finishing in 56–63 days; outdoors, plants can reach 5–8 ft and come off in September. Expect rewarding yields around 400 g/m2 inside and near 550 g per plant outside when dialed in. The effect opens bright and energetic, sharpening creativity and lifting mood before settling into a smooth, collected calm that never feels heavy. Buds often show lime-to-deep-green calyxes with touches of purple and a snowfall of trichomes, echoing the lineage: Chocolate Kush x Gelato 41. Offered in seed form by Crop King Seeds, this dessert-forward cultivar captures indulgent flavor in a balanced, easy-to-grow package.

name: Oregon Diesel
description: Born for the damp chill of the Pacific Northwest, Oregon Diesel marries NYC Diesel and Blackberry in a hardy, indica-dominant hybrid from Homegrown Natural Wonders. Dense, pebble-shaped flowers flush dark green to violet and sparkle with frost, releasing a diesel core laced with ripe berry and crisp pine. Caryophyllene leads the terpene stack, with limonene and pinene rounding a fuel-and-fruit profile that translates cleanly to the palate. Typical batches test around 14–22% THC with trace CBD, delivering an evening-leaning, clear-headed calm that softens into full-body ease, happy mood, and easy sleep. Plants stay compact with minimal stretch, making canopy control simple; outdoors they shrug off cooler nights and fall moisture. Expect a swift 7–8 week bloom (about 49–56 days), medium yields inside, and notably higher returns outside where root space and sun are abundant. The Blackberry parent lends color and a jammy sweetness, while NYC Diesel sharpens the edges with grapefruit-gassy lift — together producing a balanced, soothing ride without muddiness. First showcased by Homegrown Natural Wonders and later popularized by Oregon cultivators, Oregon Diesel remains a reliable, climate-tolerant workhorse that trades flash for consistency, aromatic depth, and end-of-day relaxation. Structure is squat and sturdy with tight internodes, stacked calyxes, and dense colas that trim easily when dried.

name: Durban Dawg

Expect a clean, forest-fresh nose where berry sweetness threads through pine sap and a pungent diesel-tinged finish; on the palate it stays crisp and coniferous before turning faintly fruity. Myrcene, caryophyllene, and limonene headline the terpene bill, steering an energetic, creative, and talkative mood that arrives almost as fast as you exhale yet stays composed rather than jittery. Plants show early vertical vigor, stacking into spear-like colas with medium density and excellent trichome coverage; tall canopies benefit from training. Indoors, flowering typically wraps in 63-70 days, with dialed rooms returning medium-high yields around 450-550 g/m2; outdoors, robust plants can top a meter and a half when given full sun. Potency commonly sits in the low 20s, with THC around 22-23% and negligible CBD, translating to clear, buoyant effects and a tidy comedown. Whether you chase focus for daytime projects or simply enjoy vintage Durban sparkle polished by modern Chemdog lineage, Durban Dawg delivers classic drive wrapped in vivid, terpene-rich character. Growers rate difficulty as medium; height trends tall indoors and taller outside with proper support.

name: Tidebanger
description: Wizard Trees' Tidebanger rolls in like a clean, rising swell, born from Tide (a Blue Zushi expression of Zkittlez x Kush Mints) and Sherbanger #22 (Sunset Sherbet x Headbanger). Batches typically land in the mid-to-upper 20s for THC with negligible CBD, delivering a bright, fast onset that blooms into euphoric uplift before settling into calm, body-centered relaxation. Breeder credit goes to Wizard Trees, who teased Tidebanger as the next wave after the celebrated Zangbanger line, aiming to fuse layered candy with real gas and sturdier structure. In the jar, lime, berry, and creamy sherb mingle with clean fuel; on the grind, the minty cool rises and clings to the palate. Phenotypes lean balanced, showing a predictable 1.5x stretch and sturdy apical dominance that makes canopies easy to steer. Dry rooms reward patience-the bouquet condenses into vivid candy-gas while the finish stays clean.

name: Pi Chew
description: Pi Chew from Ronin Seeds snaps like its namesake candy: bright, tropical and just a little wild. Bred by pairing Z-Pie #14 with Zuyaqui, this hybrid leans into dessert-forward aromatics: ripe tropical fruit, sugar-sweet candy and a light woody pine counterpoint that keeps it from turning cloying. Expect dense, lime to olive buds frosted in sticky trichomes and threaded with orange pistils, a morphology that reflects its Z-Pie-line heritage. Reported batches routinely test in the high 20s for THC (roughly 29 to 30%), with negligible CBD, translating to a feel that opens happy and euphoric before settling into an easy, deeply relaxed cruise. The terpene expression often centers on limonene and caryophyllene, sometimes supported by linalool, mapping neatly to the strain's candy citrus top notes and soft, woody echo. In the garden, Pi Chew typically stays at a manageable, medium stature and returns high yields when dialed in - think tight internodes and a tidy canopy that favors even light. Whether grown by Oregon outfits or boutique rooms elsewhere, the flavor holds: tropical candy up front, faint cream and pine underneath. With breeder credit to Ronin Seeds and lineage that blends Z-Pie's confectionary fruit with Zuyaqui's gas-and-tea nuance, Pi Chew reads like a modern classic with unmistakable character throughout.

name: Z-Chew
description: Z-Chew pairs artisan selection with pedigree punch. Bred by Ronin Seeds in collaboration with Zikigai Gardens and released as an exclusive for The Ten Co, Pi Chew #1 blends with Kaizen #18 into a modern candy-gas hybrid. The aroma opens bright and confectionary-sweet citrus and grape candy over a creamy, almost marshmallow undertone-before a late flicker of pungent diesel sneaks in. On the palate it mirrors the nose, with sweet, citrus, and grape leading, framed by soft woody spice. Expect medium-height, well-branched plants that stack dense, resin-glossed colas and finish in roughly 55-65 days; yields land in the medium range with tidy training. The effect arrives upbeat and focused, easing into a calm, contented body glow without fog, a profile often attributed to a limonene and beta-caryophyllene backbone supported by linalool. THC typically runs high while CBD stays trace-level. Parentage is clear: Pi Chew #1 brings candied tropicals and texture, while Zuyaqui and Kaizen #18 contribute Z-forward zest and structure. Selected by Zikigai Gardens for balance and expression, Z-Chew showcases why The Ten Co hunts have become synonymous with contemporary flavor and showroom bag appeal. Growers report strong trichome coverage, vivid purples under cool nights, and a jar-pleasing, long-lasting nose.
